articles.headline: Supreme Court rules 24-hour magistrate production period begins from detention
articles.title: 24-hour to produce before Magistrate starts from detention, not ‘formal arrest’: Supreme Court
articles.summary: On November 5, 2026, the Supreme Court of India ruled that the twenty-four hour timeline to present a detained individual before a Magistrate starts from the exact moment of detention rather than formal arrest. Justice Ujjal Bhuyan authored the judgment, stating that both actions restrict fundamental liberty and that Article twenty-two requires immediate release if the deadline is missed.
articles.description: The Court said fundamental rights trumped even over special laws like UAPA, PMLA, in which the right to bail was heavily restricted

articles.headline: Elon Musk reacts to Republican midterm election defeat on X
articles.title: U.S. midterm elections: Musk jokes about GOP election defeat after spending record sums on party
articles.summary: Technology billionaire Elon Musk posted a joke on the X platform on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, regarding the Republican Party defeat in the United States midterm elections. The comments followed his contribution of nearly five hundred million dollars to political efforts supporting Republican candidates in the race that saw Democrats seize control of Congress on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
articles.description: Democrats seized control of the U.S. Congress on November 3, capturing both the Senate and House of Representatives

articles.headline: Democrats win key gubernatorial races across the United States
articles.title: U.S. Midterm election Democrats win five governor races as Hinojosa, Bottoms, Haaland make history
articles.summary: Democratic candidates secured major gubernatorial victories in Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Georgia, and Wisconsin during the elections held on November 4, 2026. Several contenders achieved historic milestones, including Keisha Lance Bottoms becoming Georgia's first Black female governor and Gina Hinojosa becoming Texas's first Latina governor. Voters focused heavily on the cost of living and President Donald Trump's unpopularity, according to U.S. media projections.
articles.description: Hinojosa becomes Texas’s first Latina governor, Bottoms the first Black woman elected governor in the US, and Haaland the first Native American woman to lead a state

articles.headline: Ukraine raises death toll from Russian aid centre strike to 40
articles.title: Ukraine raises death toll from Russian strike on Zaporizhia to 40 people
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that the death toll from a Russian bomb attack on an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha rose to 40 people. The strike hit a school building and a shelter, killing four police officers and two rescue workers. The United Nations human rights mission stated the bombing likely violated international law as upcoming talks are scheduled in Abu Dhabi.
articles.description: Dozens may still be under the rubble in Komyshuvakha. Rescue efforts ongoing despite interruptions by Russian drones.

articles.headline: Key moments as Democrats sweep to victories in US midterms
articles.title: Key moments as Democrats sweep to victories in US midterms
articles.description: Democrats have been celebrating across the US after a series of victories saw them take control of both chambers.

articles.headline: South Africa holds municipal elections amid declining support for governing party
articles.title: South Africa votes as ANC faces further losses and coalition rule looms
articles.summary: South Africa held municipal elections on November 4, 2026, as growing public anger over corruption and failing services threatened the African National Congress. The ruling party fell below 50% support in 2021 and could drop further, potentially leading to unstable coalitions. President Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged governance failures while expressing optimism. Polling stations closed at 9 p.m., with results expected by Sunday.
articles.description: The ANC’s support could fall below 40%, while the Democratic Alliance is projected to gain ground in Johannesburg

articles.headline: Iran says four oil tankers destroyed by naval mines in Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says tankers destroyed after hitting mines in Hormuz
articles.summary: Four oil tankers were destroyed and caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz on November 4, 2026, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps. The incident follows U.S. strikes on Iran and warnings from President Masoud Pezeshkian that no one benefits from war. Tehran maintains control over the vital energy conduit and demands concessions from Washington before reopening the passage.
articles.description: It came a day after President Donald Trump said the United States had launched strikes on the Islamic Republic, following reports of a raid on Qeshm, the largest island in the strait

articles.headline: Four oil tankers destroyed by naval mines in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'
articles.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced on Wednesday that four oil tankers were destroyed after striking naval sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz while attempting to travel through a prohibited southern route. The announcement arrived as United States voters punished Republicans during the midterm elections, prompting Iranian parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf to state that the American public had rejected the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: "We endorse this message," Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf says, as Donald Trump acknowledges the conflict's role in the Republican Party's defeat.

articles.headline: Zelensky awards Melania Trump for humanitarian support following ceasefire agreement
articles.title: Zelensky gives Melania Trump Ukraine's highest award after Oleshky ceasefire
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky awarded the Order of Princess Olha, 1st Class, to United States First Lady Melania Trump for her humanitarian support. The recognition follows her role in securing a temporary ceasefire in Kherson that enabled evacuations from Oleshky. Russian and Ukrainian delegations are scheduled to meet at the White House on Thursday to discuss ongoing diplomatic efforts and postwar security.
articles.description: Russian and Ukrainian delegations will meet the US first lady at the White House on Thursday.

articles.headline: Trump loses control of Congress
articles.title: Trump loses control of Congress
articles.description: Democrats have made historic gains in the US midterms, dealing a major setback to President Donald Trump.

articles.headline: Global leaders react as US Democrats win control of Congress
articles.title: ‘Seismic shift’: World reacts to US midterm election results
articles.summary: Foreign governments are evaluating how Democratic control of both chambers of Congress might reshape United States foreign policy following midterm elections. Iranian officials warned against conflict, while European and Asian leaders expressed varied expectations regarding trade, defense, and international alliances. According to local reports, the political shift follows widespread voter concerns over economic pressures and ongoing military engagements.
articles.description: Iran's top negotiator says US voters sent a “NO TO WAR” message, as Trump's Democratic opponents take Congress.

articles.headline: Democrats win US House majority in midterm elections against Trump
articles.title: Democrats win U.S. House in growing midterms wave against Trump
articles.summary: The Democratic Party secured control of the United States House of Representatives in elections on Tuesday, delivering a sharp rebuke to President Donald Trump. Growing public discontent over inflation, tariffs, and military action against Iran fueled a broad electoral wave, granting the opposition legislative power to block agendas and launch investigations.
articles.description: A Democratic House majority would give the Opposition the power to block Mr. Trump’s legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration during the final two years of his presidency

articles.headline: Democrats win control of House and Senate in midterms
articles.title: Democrats win control of House and Senate: Key US midterms takeaways
articles.summary: During the November 2026 elections, the Democratic Party won control of both the United States House of Representatives and the Senate, dealing a major defeat to President Donald Trump's Republicans. According to the Associated Press, Democrats secured significant victories nationwide, including historic wins such as Michigan electing its first Muslim senator, Abdul El-Sayed.
articles.description: This is the first time in 20 years that a Republican president has lost both houses of US Congress.

articles.headline: Georgia elects first Black woman governor in US
articles.title: Georgia elects first Black woman governor in US
articles.description: Al Jazeera’s Matthew Torres reports on the historic gubernatorial election win in Georgia.

articles.headline: Democrats sweep US midterms to secure full control of Congress
articles.title: Democrats deliver a historic routing to Republicans in US midterms
articles.summary: United States voters delivered a historic rebuke to President Donald Trump during Tuesday midterm elections, handing Democrats control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate after flipping multiple seats across the country. Economic grievances regarding high petrol and grocery prices, which surged following the launch of a war on Iran in February, heavily drove the voter backlash against the Republican Party.
articles.description: For the first time in nearly 30 years, a Democrat will now represent South Carolina in the US Senate.

articles.headline: Democrats capture Congress in midterm upset and outline priorities
articles.title: Democrats win Congress: How they did it, and what it means
articles.summary: The Democratic Party secured comfortable majorities in both the Senate and the House of Representatives during the United States midterm elections, flipping multiple critical seats. While the newly achieved legislative control empowers Democrats to block presidential appointments and launch congressional investigations, President Donald Trump has already signalled his intention to utilize his veto power extensively against their policy agenda.
articles.description: With control of Congress, Democrats can challenge Trump’s agenda through subpoenas, confirmation votes.

articles.headline: Democratic Party gains US House majority in 2026 midterm elections
articles.title: Democratic Party gains US House majority in 2026 midterm elections
articles.summary: Following the midterm elections, the Democratic Party has secured control of the United States House of Representatives after gaining five seats. The victory positions New York Representative Hakeem Jeffries to potentially become the speaker of the House, succeeding Republican Mike Johnson. The newly elected 120th Congress is scheduled to be sworn in on January 3, 2027, ending a period of Republican unified power in Washington, DC.
articles.description: All 435 seats in the lower chamber of Congress were on the ballot in Tuesday's midterm race.

articles.headline: Democrat James Talarico wins Texas Senate seat in midterm setback
articles.title: In huge blow to Republicans, Democrat Talarico flips U.S. Senate seat in Texas
articles.summary: Democrat James Talarico defeated Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton on Tuesday, flipping a Republican Senate seat in a major blow to the party. The nationwide midterm vote served as a referendum on President Donald Trump, with voter discontent over rising living costs, tariffs, and the military conflict with Iran weighing heavily on Republican candidates.
articles.description: Democrats notched a string of early victories in U.S. midterm elections, flipping a Republican-held Senate seat and making inroads in conservative House districts as President Donald Trump faced the prospect of a bruising election setback

articles.headline: Keisha Lance Bottoms becomes Georgia’s first black governor
articles.title: Keisha Lance Bottoms becomes Georgia’s first black governor
articles.description: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected Governor-elect of Georgia becoming the state's first black governor

articles.headline: Trump and Republicans trampled in the midterms
articles.title: Trump and Republicans trampled in the midterms
articles.description: Al Jazeera’s Alan Fisher says Republicans are facing a worse-than-expected midterm performance.

articles.headline: Iran dismisses US response to Hormuz terms as Trump confirms strikes
articles.title: Iran says US reply to Hormuz plan ‘unconvincing’; Trump confirms strikes
articles.summary: Iran rejected the United States response to its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz as unconvincing on Tuesday, while US President Donald Trump confirmed launching defensive strikes on Qeshm Island. Meanwhile, commercial shipping faced renewed threats as projectiles struck a tanker near Oman and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed four tankers hit mines.
articles.description: Indirect talks continue as Trump says US military struck an Iranian anti-aircraft facility on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Democratic Party regains control of US Senate in midterm elections
articles.title: Democratic Party wins US Senate in 2026 midterm elections
articles.summary: The Democratic Party secured a majority in the United States Senate during the 2026 midterm elections on Tuesday, ending the Republican legislative trifecta. Democrats achieved crucial net gains across several states, including surprise victories in traditional Republican strongholds like Texas and Kansas, while incumbent senators successfully defended seats in key swing states.
articles.description: The outcome is widely seen as a rebuke to Trump's Republican Party, which won control of the chamber in 2024.

articles.headline: Scepticism as Trump says he’s ending Israel’s $3.8 bn military aid deal
articles.title: Scepticism as Trump says he’s ending Israel’s $3.8 bn military aid deal
articles.description: US President Donald Trump says he plans to stop the annual $3.8bn military aid package to Israel by the end of the year.

articles.headline: First polls close in pivotal US midterm elections
articles.title: First polls close in pivotal US midterm elections
articles.summary: Voting has concluded in the crucial United States midterm elections, determining control of Congress with all House seats and thirty-five Senate seats contested. Democrats seek to regain power amid cost of living concerns. Kentucky's sixth district provided early results, featuring Navy veteran Zach Dembo and Republican Ralph Alvarado, with nationwide outcomes expected through Wednesday.
articles.description: With control of the US Congress on the line, results from Tuesday's races will have marked implications for the country.

articles.headline: Spanish transport minister resigns following deadly train crash in Urda
articles.title: Spanish transport minister resigns days after deadly train crash
articles.summary: Spain's Transport Minister Ãscar Puente stepped down six days after a high-speed train collision resulted in sixty-nine fatalities and numerous injuries near Urda. Making the announcement in Congress on Tuesday evening, Puente stated that remaining in office after two major rail accidents in under a year was untenable. The tragedy occurred when a Renfe service struck a stationary Iryo train.
articles.description: At least 69 people were killed and dozens injured in the collision south of the capital, Madrid.

articles.headline: Democrats win congressional majorities following voter backlash against Donald Trump
articles.title: Democrats vow to rein in Donald Trump as he shows off White House ballroom
articles.summary: Following voter anger over living costs and the United States-Iran war, Democrats secured majorities in the Senate and House of Representatives during the November 2026 midterm elections. The historic defeat marks the first time President Donald Trump will face opposition control in both congressional chambers, potentially leading to legislative deadlock and investigations into his administration, while Republican leaders and Vice President J.D. Vance acknowledged the war played a role in the losses.
articles.description: It will be the first time ⁠that Mr. Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with Democrats controlling both chambers of Congress

articles.headline: North Korea signals reluctance for summit with U.S. President Donald Trump
articles.title: Donald Trump’s midterm defeat dims hopes of North Korea meeting
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un’s sister, Kim Yo Jong, indicated Pyongyang has no interest in further dialogue with Washington, citing hostility. Analysts suggest the North Korean regime is prioritizing its nuclear arsenal and economic ties with Russia following Donald Trump’s midterm election defeat, which has left the U.S. president with limited political leverage.
articles.description: Mr. Kim’s powerful sister Kim Yo Jong signalled that there was little appetite for renewed dialogue with Washington, saying Pyongyang had “no need to sit face to face with such unreliable and hostile persons”

articles.headline: India extends five hundred million dollar credit line to Guyana
articles.title: India announces extension of $500 million line of credit for Guyana
articles.summary: During the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar announced an extension of a five hundred million dollar line of credit to Guyana for infrastructure, health, and defense projects. Meeting with Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali on Wednesday, Jaishankar also oversaw the signing of three bilateral agreements regarding small enterprises, quick impact projects, and digital public infrastructure cooperation.
articles.description: EAM Jaishankar met Guyanese President Mohamed Irfaan Ali on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting

articles.headline: Joshua Wong sentenced to ten years in prison under Hong Kong security law
articles.title: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
articles.summary: Pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong was sentenced to ten years in prison on November 5, 2026, for colluding with foreign forces under Hong Kong's national security law. Having already spent six years behind bars for previous convictions, the thirty-year-old co-founder of the defunct political party Demosisto received the latest sentence after pleading guilty in September to charges related to lobbying foreign governments.
articles.description: Wong, 30, is among hundreds of Hongkongers detained under the controversial national security law.

articles.headline: Hong Kong court sentences pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to ten additional years
articles.title: Hong Kong democracy activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in jail
articles.summary: Hong Kong High Court Judge William Tam sentenced pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to ten additional years in prison after finding him guilty of colluding with foreign entities under the national security law. Wong, who pleaded guilty in September, was already serving time for previous protest-related offenses and faced condemnation from foreign governments and rights organizations including Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch following the ruling.
articles.description: Wong, in prison since 2020, was found guilty of colluding with foreign entities in violation of national security law.

articles.headline: Americans vote in midterm elections determining presidential power
articles.title: U.S. midterm election results 2026: List of key winners
articles.summary: Americans went to the polls on November 3, 2026, in midterm elections that will determine how much power United States President Donald Trump retains for the remainder of his term. Voters decided all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats, and 36 state governorships. Over 210 million registered citizens were eligible to cast ballots across the country as voting concluded.
articles.description: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats, and governorships in 36 states went for election, with about 210 million people registered to vote

articles.headline: Global emissions remain high as Paris Agreement marks ten years
articles.title: Ten years of the Paris Agreement: Has the world kept its climate promises?
articles.summary: Celebrating ten years since its entry into force, the Paris Agreement has successfully driven clean energy expansion, though global greenhouse gas emissions remain near record highs and scientists warn that the one point five degree Celsius warming limit will likely be surpassed soon. China, the United States, and India continue to produce over half of annual emissions, and despite national climate policies reducing projections to about two point six degrees of warming by twenty one hundred, current reductions remain too slow.
articles.description: Nearly 200 countries pledged to limit warming to 1.5C. We look at who has delivered and who has fallen short.

articles.headline: Supreme Court bans illegal detentions and orders normal transit operations in Delhi
articles.title: Supreme Court bars illegal detention as lawyers cite Emergency
articles.summary: During an extraordinary Sunday hearing, Supreme Court Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana ordered the Union government and the Delhi Police to halt illegal detentions and restore normal public transport, internet access, and movement around Delhi following a massive security clampdown. Senior lawyers compared the police actions to the nineteen seventy-five Emergency, while Solicitor General Tushar Mehta defended the government actions and agreed to file an affidavit addressing the restrictions.
articles.description: Court seeks affidavits on Metro curbs and alleged violations of its October 9 order

articles.headline: Tanvi Patri becomes first Indian player in Youth Olympic badminton final
articles.title: Tanvi Patri becomes first Indian badminton player to reach Youth Olympic badminton final
articles.summary: Fifteen-year-old Tanvi Patri from Odisha made history by defeating Japan's Yuzuno Watanabe twenty-one to fourteen, eleven to twenty-one, and twenty-one to nineteen during a fifty-four minute semifinal. The victory makes her the first Indian badminton player to reach the women's singles final at the Youth Olympic Games, where she will face China's Yi Xin Zhang for the gold medal.
articles.description: The 15-year-old from Odisha continued her impressive run, stunning Japan’s second seed, Yuzuno Watanabe, 21-14, 11-21, 21-19, in a hard-fought 54-minute semifinal to book her place in the title clash

articles.headline: Markets surge on falling oil prices and United States midterm election results
articles.title: Markets on spree after crude tumbles 9% following Trump’s midterm fallout
articles.summary: Stock market indices Sensex and Nifty recorded sharp gains in early trading on November 5, 2026, driven by a ten percent drop in crude oil prices and investor optimism following the United States midterm elections. American voters handed control of Congress to the Democratic Party, raising hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the West Asia conflict and easing inflationary pressures across international markets.
articles.description: Analysts suggest that the sharp decline in oil prices and the opening up of the Strait of Hormuz are anchoring the Indian markets

articles.headline: U.S. midterm elections feature historic firsts for governors and senators
articles.title: U.S. midterm elections witness historic firsts: First Black woman governor to first Muslim senator
articles.summary: Voters across the United States elected several groundbreaking candidates during the November 3, 2026, midterm elections. Keisha Lance Bottoms won Georgia as the first Black female governor, Deb Haaland became New Mexico's first Native American female governor, Abdul El-Sayed won a Senate seat in Michigan as the first Muslim senator, Chris Pappas became the first openly gay male senator in New Hampshire, and Peggy Flanagan secured a Senate seat as the first Native American female senator.
articles.description: The US midterm elections delivered a series of historic firsts by electing a Black female governor, a Muslim senator and openly gay male US senator

articles.headline: President Donald Trump halts military aid to Israel amid midterm fallout
articles.title: Midterm results put U.S.-Israel ties under further strain
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced on election day that Washington will end approximately four billion dollars in annual military aid to Israel by the end of the year. Citing political costs and the success of Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, the decision places additional strain on diplomatic relations between the two long-standing allies in West Asia.
articles.description: Critics on both sides argue that Mr. Netanyahu pulled Mr. Trump into a war he could not win. Now when even the Vice-President is blaming the war for the electoral defeat, the real target is the ‘special relationship’ with Israel

articles.headline: BJP booth level agents deny filing voter deletion forms in Mustafabad
articles.title: Who filed 77% of Form 7s in Delhi’s Mustafabad? BJP BLAs named as ‘objectors’ deny them
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party booth level agents named as objectors in seventy-seven percent of deletion applications in Delhi’s Mustafabad constituency denied association with the filings. The Hindu reported that sixteen of twenty registered agents denied submitting Form seven applications targeting Muslim electors since August thirty-first, two thousand twenty-six. The applications allegedly violated an Election Commission of India cap introduced on October ninth, two thousand twenty-six.
articles.description: Of the 20 BJP-appointed Booth Level Agents named in 787 deletion applications, 16 deny submitting or signing the forms, while one says he filed “over 500”

articles.headline: Indian government overhauls Agnipath recruitment scheme with extended service options
articles.title: What are the changes in Agniveer scheme, and what prompted government to implement them? | Explained
articles.summary: The Indian Cabinet approved a major overhaul of the Agnipath recruitment scheme on November 4, 2026. Based on recommendations from the three armed services, the policy grants Agniveers not initially selected for regular service an additional two years of engagement, establishing a clear pathway for all willing personnel to eventually join the military as regular soldiers.
articles.description: The decision, approved by the Cabinet on the recommendations of the three services, creates a pathway for the eventual absorption of all willing Agniveers, subject to merit and prescribed selection criteria

articles.headline: Vice President J D Vance blames administration policies for Republican midterm rout
articles.title: Vance eyes own trail in America First politics in Republican rout
articles.summary: United States Vice President J.D. Vance stated that the administration, rather than the electorate, abandoned America First principles and caused the Republican midterm election losses. Highlighting the war on Iran as a primary factor, Mr. Vance's public disavowal strengthens his position as a potential presidential contender for two thousand twenty-eight while distancing him from Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
articles.description: What continues to work for Mr. Vance is that he manages to challenge and critique Mr. Trump without triggering a meltdown from the latter. Whether he can continue in that manner all the way to the 2028 election remains to be seen. But Mr. Vance would be perfectly capable of carrying forward his own version of America First without Mr. Trump

articles.headline: CERT-In releases security guidelines for auditing autonomous artificial intelligence agents
articles.title: CERT-In calls for testing AI agents for unauthorised tool use, privilege abuse
articles.summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team issued new auditing guidelines on November 5, 2026, to secure advanced artificial intelligence systems capable of autonomous tasks and tool use. The framework mandates rigorous testing for unauthorised permission usage, privilege abuse, credential misuse, memory manipulation, and multi-agent communication risks to ensure strict operational safety and accountability within production environments.
articles.description: Guidelines require checks on agents’ permissions, task delegation and emergency-stop mechanisms; multi-agent systems must maintain authenticated, logged communications and records of actions

articles.headline: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison
articles.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years in prison in 2nd national security case
articles.summary: Prominent activist Joshua Wong received a ten-year prison sentence on November 5, 2026, for his second conviction under a national security law in Hong Kong. Judge William Tam rejected claims that his role was minor and ordered the terms to be served concurrently. Critics argue the case reflects a broader crackdown on dissent, while Beijing maintains the law is essential for city stability.
articles.description: The 30-year-old is already serving a four-year, eight-month prison term for the city's biggest national security case

articles.headline: Volodymyr Zelenskyy hopes United States Democratic midterm victory increases support for Ukraine
articles.title: Zelenskyy hopes Democratic Congress will bring more US help for Ukraine
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Democratic gains in the United States midterm elections could increase military and financial assistance for Kyiv. Speaking on November 4, 2026, after voters handed Congress control to the Democrats, Zelenskyy expressed optimism that stronger American backing would influence Russian President Vladimir Putin to help end the ongoing European conflict.
articles.description: EU officials also urge new US Congress to step up pressure on Russia to end the four-and-a-half-year war.

articles.headline: Supreme Court says India fertility drop makes two-child penalties outdated
articles.title: Falling fertility rate makes two-child penalties outdated in India, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India ruled on November 4, 2026, that laws penalising individuals for having more than two children have lost relevance due to falling fertility rates. A Bench led by Justice P.S. Narasimha stated that the 2003 Javed judgment requires reconsideration as demographic shifts point toward an ageing population. The court protected an elected official from disqualification under the Maharashtra law.
articles.description: ‘The foundation of such laws, that is, the fear of overpopulation, has crumbled due to demographic changes in the past few decades’, says Bench

articles.headline: Technology giants gain following United States Democratic midterm election sweep
articles.title: U.S. Democrats' midterm sweep fuels $750 billion Big Tech rally
articles.summary: Shares of major United States technology companies surged on November 5, 2026, following the Democratic Party's midterm election sweep. Investors anticipated that potential curbs on data-centre construction could restrict overbuilding and reduce capital expenditures, boosting market values for firms such as Amazon and Apple while smaller cloud infrastructure competitors experienced significant share price declines.
articles.description: Apple, which has avoided ‌Big Tech’s massive AI spending but is feeling the sting of an AI-fueled surge in memory chip prices, jumped nearly 7% ‌to a record high

articles.headline: Mamdani: ‘it’s morning again in America’ after blue wave
articles.title: Mamdani: ‘it’s morning again in America’ after blue wave
articles.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani urged fellow Democrats to ‘fulfill promises’ after sweeping wins.

articles.headline: Paraguay bank collapses with half of population’s savings
articles.title: Paraguay bank collapses with half of population’s savings
articles.description: Protests have erupted across Paraguay after Ueno Bank was shut down in the middle of the night over a solvency crisis.

articles.headline: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to ten years in jail
articles.title: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to ten years in jail
articles.description: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong, who became the global face of Hong Kong’s pro-democracy movement has been sentenced.

articles.headline: Vice-President JD Vance blames Iran war for Republican midterm election losses
articles.title: Vance walks Trump tightrope with scathing election critique blaming Iran war
articles.summary: Vice-President JD Vance publicly attributed the Republican Party's midterm defeat to the ongoing war in Iran, marking a rare departure from President Donald Trump’s foreign policy. While Trump defended the conflict, he acknowledged its electoral impact. Analysts view Vance’s statement as a potential early move to establish a distinct platform for a 2028 presidential bid.
articles.description: The vice-president's blunt assessment of Republican election defeat marked one of the sharpest breaks with a sitting president in recent memory.

articles.headline: Syria and Saudi Arabia sign defence and financial cooperation agreements
articles.title: Syria, Saudi Arabia sign defence cooperation deal, agree $403m in loans
articles.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman signed a defence cooperation deal and secured $403 million in Saudi loans for Syrian infrastructure, energy, and healthcare. The agreements follow discussions on regional security and maritime navigation. Syria is currently evaluating potential entry into a mutual defence alliance with Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan.
articles.description: Defence cooperation deal signed as Syria's President al-Sharaa visits Riyadh for the second time in less than a month.

articles.headline: World Bank brief highlights extreme poverty decline and high prosperity gap
articles.title: From poverty alleviation to prosperity
articles.summary: According to a World Bank brief, India experienced a significant decline in extreme poverty between 2011 and 2023, with hundreds of millions moving out of poverty. However, the report highlights a high prosperity gap driven by flat real earnings, low-productivity work, and rising youth unemployment, indicating that many individuals require substantial income increases to reach prosperity.
articles.description: India has reduced extreme poverty, but its high prosperity gap shows that millions remain far from a comfortable standard of living; informal work, stagnant wages and limited employment opportunities continue to constrain upward mobility

articles.headline: U.S. midterm results and their potential impact on China relations
articles.title: What the U.S. midterms mean for ties with China
articles.summary: Democratic victories in United States midterm elections have given the party control of Congress, creating both challenges and opportunities for Beijing. Analysts suggest the shift could limit President Donald Trump's use of tariffs and revive congressional pressure for arms sales to Taiwan. Meanwhile, experts believe China will likely continue its high-level leader engagement with President Trump to manage bilateral ties.
articles.description: Here is how the outcome of the vote, which offers the Democratic Party the power to stymie President Donald Trump’s maverick foreign policy, could impact the thorny relationship between Washington and Beijing

articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate seat to become first Muslim in upper chamber.
articles.title: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed claims victory in Michigan Senate battle
articles.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed claimed victory in the Michigan United States Senate race on Wednesday, defeating Republican Mike Rogers. The forty-two-year-old physician ran on progressive policies, including universal health care, and will succeed retiring Senator Gary Peters. His historic election makes him the first Muslim American and the first Democratic doctor to serve in the upper chamber since 1969.
articles.description: El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour

articles.headline: JD Vance blames Iran war for Republican midterm election losses
articles.title: U.S. VP Vance says Iran war was the reason Republicans lost midterms
articles.summary: United States Vice-President JD Vance stated on November 4, 2026, that the Republican Party lost the midterm elections due to the Iran war. Writing on X, Mr Vance attempted to distance himself from the conflict initiated by President Donald Trump in February, noting that an honest assessment of future political strategy must acknowledge this outcome.
articles.description: The U.S. vice-president said the conflict doomed Republicans, as he sought to distance himself from the war ahead of a possible 2028 presidential run

articles.headline: J.D. Vance distances himself from Iran war after midterm losses
articles.title: Vance tries to distance himself from Iran war after Republican Party’s deep losses in midterm elections
articles.summary: United States Vice President J.D. Vance blamed the unpopular military conflict with Iran for the Republican Party suffering deep losses in the midterm elections on November 3, 2026. Breaking from President Donald Trump, who defended the war, Vance wrote on social media that voters cast ballots for Democrats due to the war and living costs. He also suggested changes to immigration enforcement.
articles.description: J.D. Vance, who has said he would decide after the election whether to run for President in 2028, issued a lengthy social media post blaming the unpopular conflict with Iran for the Grand Old Party’s drubbing

articles.headline: Trump defends Iran war despite role in Republican midterm losses
articles.title: After Republicans routed, Trump devotes first post-midterm event to White House ballroom
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated on November 4, 2026, that the military conflict with Iran was necessary to prevent Tehran from acquiring nuclear weapons, despite admitting it caused a gasoline price surge that contributed to Republican losses in the congressional midterms. Trump defended his actions to reporters, noting he would change nothing, while Vice President J.D. Vance also attributed the electoral setback to the war.
articles.description: Donald Trump said the war has been worth it to stop Tehran from “having ‌a nuclear weapon”

articles.headline: Democratic victory in United States midterm elections highlights economic pressures and voter dissatisfaction
articles.title: U.S. midterm elections: An economy under pressure, political shift and the road ahead
articles.summary: United States midterm elections delivered a political setback to President Donald Trump as Democrats secured control of the House of Representatives and the Senate. The results underline public dissatisfaction with household finances despite economic growth, as inflation accelerated to 3.7 percent in September driven largely by surging energy costs and fuel oil price increases.
articles.description: Despite robust economic growth, a buoyant stock market and relatively low unemployment, rising living costs have emerged as a major political challenge for the Trump administration

articles.headline: Vote counting underway in critical South Africa elections
articles.title: Vote counting underway in critical South Africa elections
articles.description: Votes are being counted across South Africa after a record 29.2 million people registered to vote.

articles.headline: US midterm voting begins in high-stakes test of Trump’s presidency
articles.title: US midterm voting begins in high-stakes test of Trump’s presidency
articles.description: Voting is under way across the US in midterm elections that could strip Trump’s Republicans of control of Congress.

articles.headline: Democrats capture full control of U.S. Congress in midterms
articles.title: U.S. midterm election results: Senate, House and Governor shifts before and after
articles.summary: The November 2026 U.S. midterm elections resulted in a dramatic shift as Democrats secured majorities in both the Senate and the House of Representatives, crossing the 218-seat threshold in the lower chamber. Driven by voter discontent over economic pressures and living costs, the results contrasted sharply with the 2022 midterms. Several candidates achieved historic firsts, including Abdul El-Sayed entering the Senate as the first Muslim member.
articles.description: Democrats surged to full control of Congress in the November 2026 U.S. midterm elections, flipping the Senate and House after winning net seats across key battlegrounds and sweeping into Republican strongholds. Here’s what changed between 2022 and 2026 midterms.

articles.headline: U.S. midterm results may reshape geopolitics more than bilateral ties
articles.title: U.S. midterm results may matter less for India-U.S. ties than for India’s room to manoeuvre in geopolitics
articles.summary: The outcome of the United States midterm elections is expected to have a greater impact on global geopolitics and India's operating environment than on bilateral relations. The projected Democratic majorities in the House of Representatives and the Senate mean President Donald Trump will face policy constraints, while New Delhi closely monitors potential shifts in Washington's approach to the Iran conflict following the February 2026 military attacks.
articles.description: With U.S. President Donald Trump’s Republicans facing a major loss, the results could affect India’s position on the Iran war, Russian oil, the trade deal, immigration and China policy

articles.headline: U.S. Treasury imposes new sanctions on Indian and Turkish entities
articles.title: U.S. slaps sanctions on Indian, Turkish firms and people for aiding Iran
articles.summary: The United States Treasury issued fresh sanctions on Wednesday against individuals and companies in India and Turkiye for supporting Iran. The measures target a network run by Suniel Kumar Sharma and Jaspreet Preeti Shahid that allegedly provided false maritime certifications for vessels transporting Iranian petroleum, alongside Turkish firm Fugo Ground Services Inc for aiding Iran's aviation sector.
articles.description: The sanctions are part of the Trump administration’s “Operation Economic Outcast,” which aims to cut off Iran’s ability to sell oil to fund the war with the U.S. and Israel

articles.headline: Five Republican election deniers defeated in key state gubernatorial races
articles.title: Election deniers lose races for governor in key US swing states
articles.summary: Five Republican candidates who cast doubt on the 2020 presidential election lost their bids for governor in crucial battleground states following Democratic gains in the midterm elections. The defeats occurred in Arizona, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, and Georgia. The outcome could significantly impact the political landscape ahead of the 2028 presidential race.
articles.description: State leaders can hold significant sway over election administration, with implications for the 2028 presidential race.

articles.headline: Israeli President Herzog accepts election results and begins coalition talks
articles.title: Israel’s Herzog accepts vote results, opens talks on forming a government
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has accepted certified parliamentary election results and started consultations with party leaders to form a new government. The vote resulted in neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot securing a majority. President Herzog urged political factions to compromise to avoid holding another election early next year.
articles.description: Move deals blow to Netanyahu's efforts to discredit the elections, in which he and his allies lost their majority.

articles.headline: Trump announces US will halt financial aid to Israel by year-end
articles.title: Trump says US will stop giving Israel aid after year-end
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated in an interview that Washington will stop providing annual funding to Israel by the end of the year because the nation no longer requires assistance. Trump mentioned a prior agreement with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding the $4bn yearly aid package, though he noted help would be offered if necessary.
articles.description: Military aid to Israel and campaign contributions from Israel’s backers to US candidates have animated political debate.

articles.headline: Ohio’s voters tell Republicans: don’t take us for granted
articles.title: Ohio’s voters tell Republicans: don’t take us for granted
articles.description: Democrats flipped a Senate seat and recaptured the governor’s mansion in Ohio.

articles.headline: Democrats win congressional majorities in midterm elections but face legislative hurdles
articles.title: Democrats won Congress. But can they deliver on their promises?
articles.summary: Following midterm victories giving Democrats control of both chambers of Congress, lawmakers face significant challenges in implementing their platform without Republican cooperation or immunity from presidential vetoes. Analysts suggest Democrats may leverage investigative powers and budget legislation to address healthcare costs and scrutinise administration policies, while experts debate the realistic legislative outcomes achievable over the next two years.
articles.description: Despite their midterm election victories, Democrats face major obstacles to reining in Trump on Iran, tariffs and more.

articles.headline: Historic firsts redraw US political map in 2026 midterm elections
articles.title: Historic firsts redraw US political map in 2026 midterm elections
articles.description: The 2026 US midterms delivered a wave of historic firsts for women, Black, Muslim, gay and Native American politicians.

articles.headline: Ethiopia orders Sudanese diplomats to leave and shuts Asosa consulate
articles.title: Ethiopia expels 6 Sudan diplomats, orders closure of consulate, reports say
articles.summary: Ethiopia ordered six staff members of the Sudanese consulate in Asosa to depart within forty-eight hours and closed the diplomatic facility amid escalating bilateral tensions. The action follows Sudan filing complaints with the United Nations Security Council and the African Union accusing Ethiopia of supporting the Rapid Support Forces, allegations that Addis Ababa denies alongside counter-claims regarding regional rebels.
articles.description: Move comes after Sudan lodged official complaints against Ethiopia, accusing Addis Ababa of supporting the RSF group.

articles.headline: US launches limited military strikes on Iran ahead of midterm elections
articles.title: US strikes Iranian island ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: United States forces launched limited military strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, according to officials speaking to CBS. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported explosions following the operation, which President Donald Trump described as a response to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps firing on an aircraft. The developments occur ahead of congressional elections that will determine party control of the United States legislature.
articles.description: US officials described the attacks on Qeshm Island as limited and defensive, according to CBS, the BBC's US partner.

articles.headline: Trump blames Iran war for midterms losses
articles.title: Trump blames Iran war for midterms losses
articles.description: President Donald Trump said the war in Iran likely contributed to Republican setbacks in the midterm elections

articles.headline: Polls open across United States for pivotal 2026 midterm elections
articles.title: Polls open in closely contested US midterm elections 2026
articles.summary: Voters across the United States headed to the polls on Tuesday for critical midterm elections involving all 435 House seats and 35 Senate positions. More than 57 million Americans already cast early ballots in major battleground states. Republicans currently hold narrow majorities in both chambers, while Democrats campaign on economic issues and foreign policy changes.
articles.description: Democrats are eyeing historic gains in the US Congress that could change the trajectory of the country.

articles.headline: Police bodycam captures double-tap bombing sequence in Ukrainian village
articles.title: Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing
articles.summary: Ukrainian national police released bodycam footage documenting the aftermath of Russian glide bomb strikes that killed at least forty people in Kamyshuvakha. The video recorded by an officer showed residents entering an underground shelter before a second explosion occurred on November second, two thousand twenty-six. President Volodymyr Zelensky stated nine aerial bombs hit the location where citizens gathered for humanitarian aid.
articles.description: At least 40 people were killed and another 30 may still be under the rubble after Monday's attack on a Ukrainian village, Kyiv says.

articles.headline: Israeli President Isaac Herzog urges political compromise following divisive October 27 election
articles.title: Israel President urges compromise after divisive election
articles.summary: Following the October 27 election, Israeli President Isaac Herzog commenced meetings with party leaders on November 4, 2026, to determine who will form a government in a deeply polarised parliament. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu alleged foreign election interference, while rival Gadi Eisenkot received an endorsement from the Arab-Israeli party Raam. The Central Elections Committee reported no evidence of integrity breaches after auditing 9,069 polling stations.
articles.description: President Isaac Herzog began meeting party leaders to decide whether to give Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government in the deeply polarised country

articles.headline: Human rights organisation claims Israel restricts medical travel for child amputees in Gaza
articles.title: Israel restricting treatment for 1,100 child amputees in Gaza: NGO
articles.summary: The Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor reported on Wednesday that 1,134 children in Gaza have undergone limb amputations due to Israeli attacks, but travel restrictions and closed crossings prevent them from seeking specialized treatment abroad. According to the World Health Organization, only 500 out of 2,300 assessed amputees received permanent prosthetics between September 2024 and May 2026, amid severe shortages of certified professionals and manufacturing equipment in the strip.
articles.description: Israeli restrictions on travel and medical evacuations prevent children in Gaza from being treated abroad.

articles.headline: Americans vote in U.S. midterms that are seen as a referendum on Trump
articles.title: Americans vote in U.S. midterms that are seen as a referendum on Trump
articles.description: Americans are heading to the polls for a high-stakes midterm election on November 3, 2026, serving as a critical nationwide referendum on President Donald Trump’s administration. Amid a deeply divided political landscape defined by foreign conflict, inflation, and trade battles, voters are deciding all 435 House seats, 37 Senate seats, and 36 gubernatorial races, featuring several prominent Indian American candidates.

articles.headline: Iran warns of maximum deterrence as United States fears grow
articles.title: Will the US resume its attacks on Iran?
articles.summary: Tehran warned that its response to potential United States military action would lack geographical restrictions as fears grew regarding a renewed conflict. President Donald Trump warned that his country could attack Iran following midterm elections in which his Republican Party lost majorities in both the House and Senate. Mediators have been attempting to broker a peace deal between the two nations.
articles.description: Tehran says it's ready with a maximum deterrence plan.

articles.headline: Iranians celebrate Democrat victory in US midterms
articles.title: Iranians celebrate Democrat victory in US midterms
articles.description: US President Donald Trump acknowledged the Republicans’ crushing defeat was partly due to the war on Iran.

articles.headline: Democrats secure early midterm victories as Donald Trump faces backlash
articles.title: Democrats win U.S. Congress in midterm rout of U.S. President Donald Trump
articles.summary: Democrats captured a Republican-held Senate seat in North Carolina and made legislative gains during midterm elections as President Donald Trump faced voter discontent over living costs, tariffs and the United States war against Iran. In Georgia, former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms won the governorship, becoming the first Black woman to hold the office and ending 24 years of Republican rule.
articles.description: The Opposition party also retained key Senate seats, while victory in Georgia’s Governor race added to mounting signs that Republicans face a difficult night

articles.headline: Hakeem Jeffries promises affordability focus after Democratic midterm victory
articles.title: Hakeem Jeffries promises ‘affordability’ focus after Democratic midterm win
articles.summary: Democratic House leader Hakeem Jeffries celebrated his party taking control of both chambers of Congress in the United States midterm elections, describing the outcome as an American tsunami. Jeffries promised a relentless effort to make life more affordable and said Democrats would focus on governing rather than seeking revenge against President Donald Trump and his political allies.
articles.description: Democratic leader says party expects at least 255 House seats and promises to deliver on affordability.

articles.headline: How US midterm results could reshape Trump’s foreign policy
articles.title: How US midterm results could reshape Trump’s foreign policy
articles.description: US midterm results could reshape Trump’s political landscape and increase congressional scrutiny of his foreign policy.

articles.headline: Democrats win control of both chambers in United States midterms
articles.title: The biggest winners and losers of the 2026 US midterms
articles.summary: Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress in the November 2026 midterm elections, delivering major setbacks to President Donald Trump and Republican allies. Historic wins included Annie Andrews flipping a Senate seat in South Carolina and Abdul El-Sayed becoming the first Muslim US senator in Michigan. Meanwhile, billionaire donor Elon Musk and candidates like Vivek Ramaswamy faced high-profile defeats.
articles.description: Historic firsts, surprise victories and expensive defeats as Democrats take control of Congress.

articles.headline: Texas AI data center expansion faces uncertainty after Democratic sweep
articles.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
articles.summary: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the United States, but recent Democratic midterm election victories, including James Talarico winning a United States Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa winning the governorship against Greg Abbott, threaten major artificial intelligence buildouts. Governor Abbott had already directed a state regulator to halt permits in September, and incoming officials have pushed for potential moratoriums on new facilities.
articles.description: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position. Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent,…

articles.headline: Federal judge blocks deportation of detained Afghans to Pakistan
articles.title: U.S. judge temporarily blocks deportation of detained Afghans to Afghanistan or Pakistan
articles.summary: Judge Valerie Caproni in New York issued a temporary order halting the United States administration from deporting detained Afghan nationals to Afghanistan or Pakistan until November 7, 2026. Immigration and Customs Enforcement informed the court it lacked flights for the removals this week. Dozens of lawmakers and advocacy groups warned that returned individuals face grave dangers and retaliation from the Taliban government.
articles.description: The order pauses planned removals until Saturday after advocates and lawmakers warned that deported Afghans could face persecution, torture or death

articles.headline: ISRO's NVS-03 satellite successfully reaches geosynchronous orbit
articles.title: NVS-03 reaches geosynchronous orbit; satellite in good health
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation announced that the NVS-03 satellite successfully reached geosynchronous orbit on November 4, 2026, following four orbit maneuvers with a cumulative liquid apogee motor engine burn of 6,164 seconds. Launched on October 30 by a geosynchronous satellite launch vehicle, the third-generation navigation satellite carries indigenous and procured atomic clocks, an L1 signal, and maintains normal health.
articles.description: ‘Four orbit manoeuvres have been successfully completed with a cumulative LAM engine burn of 6164 seconds; with this the satellite has reached Geo Synchronous Orbit at an inclination of 29.980,’ said ISRO

articles.headline: Canadian officials welcome United States midterm results for trade leverage
articles.title: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief
articles.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford and other Canadian officials expressed relief following the Democratic sweep in the United States midterm elections on November 3, 2026, viewing the outcome as a rebuke of President Donald Trump's tariffs. While United States trade ministers noted short-term policies remain unchanged, experts suggest the political shift and voter frustration over rising prices provide Canada leverage to negotiate tariff-free trade deals.
articles.description: With Canada-US trade talks back on, Tuesday’s midterm Democratic wave puts pressure on the White House to come to a deal.

articles.headline: Democrats prepare for legislative challenges after winning control of Congress
articles.title: What Democrats can and can't do with their new power after taking Congress
articles.summary: Democrats secured control of both congressional chambers in the midterm elections, but face significant hurdles in enacting their agenda due to President Donald Trump’s veto power. While the party plans to investigate corruption and address healthcare costs, experts warn of potential legislative gridlock. Democrats remain divided on whether to pursue impeachment against the president.
articles.description: Democrats can vote legislation through. But Trump still has veto power.

articles.headline: Russian attacks disrupt Kyiv power as village death toll reaches forty
articles.title: Russian attacks disrupt power in Kyiv, while death toll in a stricken village rises to 40
articles.summary: Russian strikes caused extensive power and water outages across Kyiv while President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported the death toll in Komyshuvakha rose to forty. Attacks involving guided bombs targeted a former school and shelter in the Zaporizhzhia region on November second, two thousand twenty-six. Ukrainian air forces reported intercepting two hundred seventy-two drones amid ongoing regional conflict and international diplomatic meetings in Brussels.
articles.description: Russia attacked overnight with 310 drones, including 81 jet-powered drones, according to Ukraine’s air force. In its daily social media report, the air force said it downed or suppressed 272 drones of various types

articles.headline: Netanyahu and Trump allies face political defeats after midterms and elections
articles.title: Netanyahu bet on Trump – but both lost
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump lost control of Congress and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured only fifty-three coalition seats following recent electoral contests. Analysts linked the setbacks to voter backlash against the joint United States and Israeli military campaign against Iran initiated in late February. The outcomes highlighted mounting political costs associated with Washington's military and diplomatic backing of Israel.
articles.description: Israel's political establishment grapples with US voter rejection of White House ally and own contribution towards it.

articles.headline: Americans vote in midterm elections serving as referendum on Trump
articles.title: U.S. votes for midterm elections, seen as referendum on Trump
articles.summary: Citizens across the United States cast ballots on Tuesday in congressional elections deciding control of the House of Representatives and Senate during the final two years of President Donald Trump's second term. The nationwide vote encompasses all 435 House seats, 37 Senate seats, and numerous gubernatorial races. Pre-poll forecasts suggest the Democratic Party could capture the House, potentially constraining the administration's policy agenda.
articles.description: The polling will decide whether President Trump’s Republican Party retains control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, the two chambers of the U.S. Congress, or, as opinion polls are predicting, the Democratic Party wrests control of at least the House if not the Senate, also in the final two years of Mr. Trump’s second term in office

articles.headline: India secures 400 billion dollars in renewable energy investment commitments
articles.title: India secures $400-bn investment commitments in renewables; ALMM review in 15 days
articles.summary: Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi announced on November 4, 2026, that India secured preliminary investment commitments worth 400 billion dollars for renewables. Speaking at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo, Joshi also stated the government will consult industry stakeholders within 15 days regarding the potential extension of the domestic solar manufacturing framework known as ALMM.
articles.description: Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy told reporters that overseas investors have exuded confidence in India being a safe place for their investments.

articles.headline: UN commission report finds ongoing genocide and war crimes in Gaza
articles.title: United Nations report says genocide continues in Gaza
articles.summary: The Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory reported to the United Nations General Assembly on October 14, 2026, that Israeli authorities and forces continue to commit war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide in Gaza and the West Bank following the October 2025 ceasefire, citing thousands of deaths and systematic violations.
articles.description: The Israeli violations include widespread or systematic attacks directed against the civilian population, state policy, and the fact that the security forces knew the acts constituted part of an attack against the civilian population and so intended them (mens rea)

articles.headline: Vice President JD Vance blames Iran conflict for Republican midterm losses
articles.title: Presidential hopeful Vance appears to question Iran war after polls debacle
articles.summary: United States Vice President JD Vance attributed his party's midterm congressional defeat to the ongoing conflict with Iran. Writing on social media, Vance suggested the war was not worth losing Senate control to Democrats, diverging from President Donald Trump who expressed no regrets about launching the military campaign. Polling data indicated ending the conflict and altering relations with Israel were primary motivations for voters switching parties.
articles.description: US VP Vance cites trusted pollster saying Iran war, Israel ties were top of mind for Trump voters swinging to Democrats.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rejects plea for rotation of reserved parliamentary seats
articles.title: Supreme Court rejects plea for rotation of SC/ST-reserved seats in Parliament, Assemblies
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 4, 2026, refused to entertain a petition seeking mandatory rotation of constituencies reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Parliament and State Assemblies. A Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant stated that such policy decisions lie within the legislative domain of Parliament rather than the judiciary, upholding Section 9(1)(c) of the Delimitation Act, 2002.
articles.description: In a lighter vein, the CJI remarked that the petitioner could also take up the issue through public protests and demonstrations

articles.headline: Ukrainian drone strikes kill three and damage power grid in Russia
articles.title: Ukrainian strikes kill three in Russia’s Belgorod region
articles.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes killed three people in Russia's Belgorod region and targeted critical energy infrastructure across multiple regions on Wednesday, according to officials. The attacks triggered extensive power and water outages in Kyiv and parts of Russian-occupied Crimea, while Russian forces responded with strikes on Ukrainian power generation facilities.
articles.description: Russian strikes also cut power to Ukrainian cities as Moscow claims 700 Ukrainian drones downed across multiple regions.

articles.headline: Israel President Herzog begins coalition consultations after undecided election results
articles.title: Israel's president begins consultations with parties after election deadlock
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog started political consultations on Wednesday to select a candidate to form a new coalition government following the October 27 general election that produced no clear parliamentary majority. Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg delivered the official results in Jerusalem amid an ongoing Shin Bet investigation into foreign interference.
articles.description: Herzog warns politicians that "not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled" if they want to avoid another election.

articles.headline: Israeli President accepts certified election results amid fraud claims
articles.title: Israel’s President accepts certified election results in a blow to Netanyahu’s claim of vote fraud
articles.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog officially accepted the certified results of the recent parliamentary elections on November 4, 2026, dismissing unsubstantiated fraud claims made by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The election commission reported no evidence of irregularities affecting the vote outcome, where Netanyahu's bloc lost its majority. Herzog will now consult with party representatives to initiate the process of forming a new coalition government.
articles.description: Herzog's acceptance of the results as valid dealt a blow to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's effort to discredit the vote in which his religious-nationalist bloc lost its majority in the Israeli parliament, or Knesset

articles.headline: Democratic voters celebrate El-Sayed’s Michigan win in election ‘blue wave’
articles.title: Democratic voters celebrate El-Sayed’s Michigan win in election ‘blue wave’
articles.description: Democratic voters danced as they celebrated Abdul El-Sayed’s victory in Michigan.

articles.headline: US stock markets rise following Democratic sweep in midterm elections
articles.title: US markets rise as Democrats sweep midterm elections
articles.summary: United States stock markets advanced on Wednesday morning after Democrats secured control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections. Major indices opened higher at 9:30 am Eastern Time, boosted by President Donald Trump accepting the results, while oil prices declined and artificial intelligence sector stocks experienced mixed reactions.
articles.description: Nasdaq, Dow, and S&P 500 open higher after Democrats take control and Trump accepts results.

articles.headline: Supreme Court declines Trump request to halt California vote count
articles.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump's request to stop California counting disputed votes
articles.summary: The United States Supreme Court issued a one-line order on Monday denying a justice department request to set aside 20,000 mail-in ballots in California. Federal authorities had alleged the votes may have been issued to non-citizens, a claim questioned by state election officials who cited inaccuracies in the government lists. The ruling allows lower court decisions to stand on the eve of midterm elections determining congressional control.
articles.description: The ruling, which comes on the eve of the midterm elections, essentially ends the Trump administration's bid to disqualify the ballots in the state.

articles.headline: Iranian officials welcome US midterm losses as analysts warn of risks
articles.title: Iranian leaders welcome US midterm results, but Trump may still attack
articles.summary: Iranian authorities and state media celebrated the defeat of United States President Donald Trump's Republican Party in the congressional elections. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Iranian parliament speaker, stated that Americans rejected war through the vote. Meanwhile, experts such as Sanam Vakil of Chatham House warned that the political shift might increase diplomatic pressure while keeping limited military strikes possible over the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.description: Tehran views midterm results as a rejection of Trump's 'war on Iran', signalling US frustration with foreign policy.

articles.headline: Trump faces reduced legislative power following Democratic congressional victories
articles.title: Is Trump really a ‘lame duck’ after losing both houses of US Congress?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump is entering a divided government period after Democrats secured majorities in both houses of Congress during the midterm elections. While administration critics view the president as a lame duck with diminished influence over domestic legislation, political experts note that he retains significant executive authority and veto powers to pursue foreign policy and block opposition bills.
articles.description: Despite losing legislative control, the US president still has strong executive powers to push his agenda forward.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to hear Delhi voter roll exclusion case on November 19
articles.title: Delhi SIR: SC tells excluded voters not to fear prosecution even as ECI still insists on Form 6
articles.summary: Advocate Prashant Bhushan stated on November 4, 2026, that the Election Commission of India continued requiring excluded voters from Delhi's electoral rolls to complete Form 6 meant for new applicants. Petitioners Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri previously argued that forcing pre-existing voters to misrepresent themselves carries imprisonment risks. The Chief Justice of India assured that the Supreme Court is addressing the matter and scheduled the next hearing for November 19, 2026.
articles.description: On October 28, the Supreme Court made it clear that the ECI was in “error” to force pre-existing voters, deleted from the electoral rolls, to apply as new voters under Form 6 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960

articles.headline: Union Cabinet extends Agniveer military service tenure by two years
articles.title: Agnipath scheme revised, 75% of Agniveers to get two-year extension
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a two-year extension for personnel serving under the Agnipath recruitment initiative, as announced by Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani. Twenty-five percent of soldiers will continue to be absorbed into regular forces after four years, while remaining troops receive an additional engagement period before final selection evaluations. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stated that the structural reforms aim to maintain a technologically equipped military.
articles.description: 25% of Agniveers will continue to be offered regular employment in the Defence Forces on merit, as originally envisaged under the Agnipath scheme, says General N. S. Raja Subramani

articles.headline: Four killed in gunfight between rival armed groups in Manipur
articles.title: Four killed in gunfight between rival armed groups in Manipur
articles.summary: At least four individuals died and several others sustained injuries during a violent clash involving rival armed factions in Manipur's Noney district on November 4, 2026. District officials reported that the exchange of fire began at around 3:30 a.m. in Taodaijang village. Meanwhile, a tribal organization extended a regional shutdown to protest a separate security failure involving the deaths of two youths.
articles.description: The pre-dawn incident, which is said to have involved three different groups, occurred in Noney district’s Taodaijang village

articles.headline: James Talarico wins Texas Senate seat in historic midterm upset for Democrats
articles.title: James Talarico becomes first Democrat to win Texas Senate seat since 1988
articles.summary: Securing a major victory in Texas, Democrat James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton in what marked the first time a Democrat won a US Senate seat in the state since 1988. The high-profile contest became the most expensive US Senate race in history, with substantial spending from outside groups. Talarico campaigned heavily on the rising cost of living under Republican leadership while facing an opponent backed by billionaire Elon Musk.
articles.description: "This wasn't just a tsunami, not just a referendum, but this was a bloodbath," one expert told the BBC on Democrats' historic wins in Texas.

articles.headline: Democrats win control of US Congress as midterm elections yield historic results
articles.title: Everything you need to know from the US midterm elections
articles.summary: Securing majorities in both the Senate and House of Representatives during the midterm elections, Democrats took control of Congress for the remainder of President Donald Trump's term. Significant victories included Roy Cooper flipping a Senate seat in North Carolina and Keisha Lance Bottoms becoming Georgia's first Black female governor. Meanwhile, outgoing President Trump conceded that opposition candidates performed well and expressed willingness to work alongside them.
articles.description: Democrats secured some big wins - and a few historic firsts - earning congratulations from President Trump.

articles.headline: Republicans suffer major losses in United States midterm elections
articles.title: How big is the Republican midterms loss, and is there a silver lining?
articles.summary: The Republican Party experienced a severe defeat in the United States midterm elections, losing control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate to the Democratic Party. Democrats secured 228 seats in the lower chamber and 54 seats in the upper chamber, according to election results. Numerous candidates endorsed by President Donald Trump were defeated in key battleground states, though Republicans still maintained victories in several regional strongholds.
articles.description: The Republicans haven't been this weakened in Congress since 1990, but they did have some wins.

articles.headline: Pia Dandiya wins U.S. House seat from Florida
articles.title: Pia Dandiya, first-generation Indian-American, wins U.S. House of Representatives seat from Florida
articles.summary: Pia Dandiya secured a victory in the United States House of Representatives election for Florida’s 22nd congressional district on November 3, 2026. Defeating Republican opponent Casey Askar with 51.9 percent of the vote, the former high school principal and first-generation American flipped the competitive seat blue. Indian American Impact Executive Director Chintan Patel congratulated her on the historic win.
articles.description: Ms. Dandiya, a former high school principal, bagged 51.9% of the votes to become the newest Indian-American U.S. congresswoman, as per the results declared

articles.headline: Republicans blame Donald Trump for congressional losses in midterm elections
articles.title: 'This is a disaster': Angry Republicans blame Trump for midterms defeat
articles.summary: Republican party members expressed intense frustration with United States President Donald Trump following midterm election losses on Tuesday, November 4, 2026. Critics argued that unpopular policies, economic concerns, and foreign conflicts cost the party control of Congress. While allies defended the president's efforts, the results have created uncertainty for the administration's agenda.
articles.description: Some Republicans tell the BBC the president's focus on his legacy and indifference to voter concerns cost them.

articles.headline: Gaza volunteer Adam Hamawy wins historic US Congress seat
articles.title: Gaza volunteer Adam Hamawy wins historic US Congress seat
articles.description: Egyptian-American surgeon Adam Hamawy has won New Jersey’s 12th Congressional District.

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Mass arrests across occupied West Bank
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Mass arrests across occupied West Bank
articles.description: Israeli forces bomb Gaza displacement camps and arrest 45 people in the occupied West Bank.

articles.headline: Iran responds to United States midterm election results and ongoing hostilities
articles.title: Iran’s Khamenei warns Trump loss at polls won’t end US hostility
articles.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned that United States policy will not change following Democratic victories in the November 2026 midterm elections. While other officials expressed optimism about the vote and opposition to the war, Khamenei stated that resistance must continue. The remarks followed significant political setbacks for President Donald Trump.
articles.description: Iranian supreme leader says US policy won't change amid Tehran 'Fight Against Global Arrogance' day rallies

articles.headline: Multiple Russian strikes kill at least 26 at Ukraine aid centre
articles.title: Multiple Russian strikes kill at least 26 at Ukraine aid centre
articles.description: At least 26 people were killed in Russian strikes on a school being used as a humanitarian aid centre.
