articles.headline: Union Cabinet approves viability gap funding scheme for energy storage
articles.title: Union Cabinet approves ₹14,500 crore VGF scheme to develop large scale energy storage in India
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet authorized a fourteen thousand five hundred crore rupee viability gap funding initiative to support grid-scale energy storage systems from 2026 to 2031. The program aims to facilitate ninety-two gigawatt-hours of fresh capacity through pumped storage and battery infrastructure. Officials stated that competitive bidding will determine project allocation while enforcing domestic manufacturing requirements for participating developers.
articles.description: The scheme is designed to provide for the development of hydro pumped storage plant (PSP) capacity, battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity, as well as alternative energy storage technologies

articles.headline: Democratic congressional majority faces limitations on checking presidential authority
articles.title: Can Democrats stop Iran war, reverse Trump’s tariffs after midterms win?
articles.summary: Following midterm election victories on Tuesday, November 4, 2026, Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress, empowering them to investigate the administration of United States President Donald Trump. However, analysts noted that legislative constraints will make it difficult to halt ongoing military actions or significantly reverse executive tariff policies before the next presidential term.
articles.description: Democrats can block Trump's legislative agenda, launch investigations but don't have the numbers to override his veto.

articles.headline: Trump admits Iran war hurt Republican vote, vows to veto ‘insane’ bills
articles.title: Trump admits Iran war hurt Republican vote, vows to veto ‘insane’ bills
articles.description: US President Donald Trump has admitted that the war on Iran contributed to Republican losses in the midterm elections.

articles.headline: US midterm results could accelerate India trade talks
articles.title: U.S. midterm elections impact on India: Faster trade deal talks and higher tariffs likely
articles.summary: Following the Democratic victory in the United States midterm elections, experts predict that President Donald Trump may increase tariff pressure on India to secure a quick trade deal. According to Ajay Srivastava of the Global Trade Research Initiative, the administration will likely utilize executive powers to demand market access concessions, while Indian negotiators may push for more favorable terms.
articles.description: Trade and geopolitical experts say that losing control of the U.S. Congress will push President Donald Trump to increase tariff pressure on India to seal a deal. Indian negotiators, for their part, will smell an opportunity

articles.headline: Google faces slower search revenue growth amid AI expansion
articles.title: Google hasn’t figured out how to make AI pay like its search engine
articles.summary: Alphabet reported that while search queries are increasing rapidly, advertising revenue growth has decelerated as artificial intelligence interactions monetize at lower rates than traditional web searches. Advertisers remain uncertain regarding how automated conversational formats will ultimately perform compared to conventional shopping links. Executives noted that ongoing infrastructure investments are driving considerable capital expenditures across the parent company.
articles.description: Search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, Google parent Alphabet said in its earnings report last week. However, Google's Search revenue growth slowed to 12 percent year over year in the third quarter, down from roughly 17 percent in the previous quarter. Meanwhile, growth in paid clicks - clicks on ads […]

articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan race to become first Muslim US senator
articles.title: ‘Call me senator’: How Abdul El-Sayed beat Trump’s hate to create history
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed secured a historic electoral victory in Michigan, defeating Republican opponent Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim member of the United States Senate. The progressive Democrat campaigned on addressing economic inequality, healthcare access, and living costs while criticizing foreign military interventions. The incoming senator previously served as executive director of the Detroit Health Department and holds degrees from the University of Michigan, Oxford, and Columbia University.
articles.description: The 42-year-old Democrat has defeated Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim senator in the US.

articles.headline: Supreme Court upholds state power to levy sales tax
articles.title: Supreme Court upholds States’ power to levy additional sales tax, says case has become academic
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India ruled on Wednesday that a 1974 Constitution Bench judgment upholding state power to impose additional sales tax or surcharges remains valid. A seven-judge bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant concluded that the long-standing legal reference had become academic because the challenged statutory provisions were replaced and the Goods and Services Tax was introduced.
articles.description: The seven-judge Bench, led by CJI Surya Kant, said the reference in the Orissa Sales Tax Act case no longer requires adjudication since the challenged provisions have been amended and GST governs the issue moving forward

articles.headline: Why Democrats may struggle to rein in Trump’s foreign policy
articles.title: Why Democrats may struggle to rein in Trump’s foreign policy
articles.description: US President Donald Trump's foreign policy agenda faces new constraints after midterm losses.

articles.headline: Delhi Police defend ex-parte prohibitive orders in Supreme Court affidavit
articles.title: 60-day prohibitive orders passed ‘ex-parte’ to prevent unrest in key capital zones: Delhi Police in Supreme Court
articles.summary: Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court detailing seven prohibitive orders issued under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita to restrict movement and public gatherings in key capital zones. The orders were enacted following July protests and prior to October demonstrations demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, which drew petitions challenging mass detentions and transport shutdowns.
articles.description: Six orders issued on August 20 or immediately before or after this date, came a month after the July 20 protests witnessed violence in New Delhi district; one of them imposes prohibitions from September 26 to November 24

articles.headline: Houthi siege on Taiz creates severe humanitarian crisis in Yemen
articles.title: Houthis’ monthlong siege on Taiz creating misery for trapped Yemenis
articles.summary: A monthlong blockade imposed by the Houthis on Taiz has severely disrupted food, fuel, and medical supplies for hundreds of thousands of residents. According to local officials, restricted access and dozens of checkpoints have escalated living costs, separated families, and prevented patients from seeking essential medical treatments outside the besieged southern Yemeni city.
articles.description: Blockade prompts warnings of a 'catastrophe' as food, water, fuel and medical supplies are unable to reach city.

articles.headline: Israel election commission certifies parliamentary vote results
articles.title: Israel vote results confirmed as election commission rejects fraud claims
articles.summary: Israel’s Central Elections Committee certified the parliamentary election results on Wednesday after reviewing 9,069 polling stations and finding no fraud. Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg rejected Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's claims of vote rigging. The Netanyahu-led bloc won 53 seats, while opposition groups and Arab-led parties secured significant numbers, leaving no faction with the 61 seats needed to govern.
articles.description: Netanyahu’s allies refused to back the result, as President Herzog began talks on who should form the next government

articles.headline: Former US contractor pleads guilty to passing classified intelligence to Ethiopia
articles.title: US contractor gave Ethiopia secrets to help kill Tigray fighters
articles.summary: Abraham Teklu Lemma admitted to transmitting classified documents and photographs to senior officials during the 2020 civil war to assist in targeting fighters. The 54-year-old former contractor utilized his IT administrator role at agencies including the State Department to extract files between 2021 and August 2023. Facing up to 22 years in prison under a plea agreement, his sentencing is scheduled for April 14, 2027, according to the US Department of Justice.
articles.description: The Ethiopian-born American citizen admitted sharing dozens of classified documents with senior Ethiopian officials.

articles.headline: President Trump acknowledges Democratic midterm gains and accepts election results
articles.title: Trump takes aim at Republicans but says Democrats did a 'good job'
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump conceded that Democrats performed well in the midterm elections after securing control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives. Speaking on November 4, 2026, Trump accepted the outcome and expressed willingness to work with Democrats, while warning that he would use his veto power against legislation he opposed and attributing some Republican losses to voter backlash over the conflict with Iran.
articles.description: He wrote on Truth Social that Republicans would have won "in a landslide" if his name had been on the ballot.

articles.headline: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race to become first Muslim senator
articles.title: Left-wing Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins in Michigan to become first Muslim senator
articles.summary: Left-wing Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan on November 4, 2026, becoming the United States' first Muslim senator. The 42-year-old former public health administrator campaigned on a platform featuring universal health care and wealth taxes, overcoming an intense campaign marked by controversy, outside spending, and a late endorsement of his opponent by primary rival Haley Stevens.
articles.description: El-Sayed bested Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim senator in US history.

articles.headline: Florida GOP redistricting strategy backfires in midterms
articles.title: GOP’s redistricting gamble backfires in Florida as Democrats hold ground
articles.summary: The Republican-led legislature in Florida saw its redrawn congressional map backfire as Democrats retained multiple seats during the midterm elections. Kathy Castor, Pia Dandiya, and Jared Moskowitz secured victories in districts that outgoing Governor Ron DeSantis and Republican lawmakers had reconfigured in April to favor the GOP, adding to broader Democratic gains nationwide.
articles.description: Trump's party dealt a setback as Republican bid to tilt Florida's House map falters on a strong night for Democrats.

articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate seat to become first Muslim US senator
articles.title: ‘Rejecting hate’: Abdul El-Sayed wins Senate seat despite racist attacks
articles.summary: Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan on Tuesday to secure a United States Senate seat, overcoming anti-Muslim attacks led by President Donald Trump and setting a historic milestone. The victory helps Democrats regain control of the upper chamber. Voters in Detroit and neighboring Dearborn turned out in large numbers to reject bigotry, focusing instead on key issues like healthcare affordability, the economy, and ending foreign wars.
articles.description: The Democrat defeats Republican Mike Rogers to win Michigan seat to become first Muslim senator-elect in US history.

articles.headline: Republicans fuming after Democrat Talarico flips Texas Senate blue
articles.title: Republicans fuming after Democrat Talarico flips Texas Senate blue
articles.description: Republicans in Texas are trying to make sense of how they lost to the Democrats for the first time in almost 40 years.

articles.headline: Democrat Troy Jackson unseats Republican Senator Susan Collins in Maine
articles.title: Democrat Troy Jackson unseats Republican Senator Susan Collins in Maine
articles.description: Democrat Troy Jackson unseats Republican Senator Susan Collins in Maine

articles.headline: Hakeem Jeffries poised to become first Black speaker of House
articles.title: Hakeem Jeffries poised to become first Black Speaker of U.S. House of Representatives
articles.summary: Democratic midterm victories have placed New York Representative Hakeem Jeffries in line to become the first Black speaker of the United States House of Representatives. Jeffries stated that his caucus would focus on affordability, protecting Medicaid, and investigating the administration of President Donald Trump. He faces the dual challenge of uniting moderate Democrats and progressive lawmakers while managing a divided government once the new Congress takes office in January.
articles.description: As Speaker, Mr. Jeffries, representing a New York ​City congressional district, would preside over a majority that will be sworn in the first week of January, taking the reins from Republicans ⁠who controlled the House for the past four years

articles.headline: Second Indian national dies from injuries sustained in Riyadh airport attack
articles.title: Second Indian national injured in Oct 10 Riyadh airport attack dies
articles.summary: According to the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia, a second Indian citizen has died in intensive care from critical injuries sustained during the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The death brings the total fatality count to 14, following an earlier strike blamed on Yemen's Houthi rebels by Saudi authorities. The embassy stated it is assisting the family with funeral arrangements or repatriation.
articles.description: Indian embassy confirms loss as death toll rises to 14

articles.headline: Palestinians return to damaged homes in Hebron following Israeli military withdrawal
articles.title: Palestinians return to ruined Hebron homes after Israel’s 10-day siege
articles.summary: Approximately 3,300 Palestinian residents have returned to Hebron in the occupied West Bank after a 10-day forced displacement caused by an Israeli military operation following the killing of two soldiers. According to municipal officials, returning families encountered widespread property destruction, looting, and infrastructure damage. The municipality estimated direct economic losses exceeded 12 million shekels daily during the siege.
articles.description: Returning Hebron residents face significant economic and structural devastation after Israeli military operation.

articles.headline: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins election to US Senate from Michigan
articles.title: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins election to US Senate from Michigan
articles.description: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed gave an impassioned victory speech as he beat Republican Mike Rogers in the Michigan senate race

articles.headline: Supreme Court seeks government response on lifelong immunity for election commissioners
articles.title: SC seeks Centre, EC response on law giving blanket, lifelong immunity to CEC, Election Commissioners
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India issued notices to the Union government and the Election Commission of India on petitions challenging Section 16 of the 2023 appointment law. Petitioners argue that granting blanket, lifelong criminal and civil immunity to the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners violates the basic structure of the constitution and judicial review powers. The court scheduled the next hearing for December 18.
articles.description: RJD MP Manoj Jha has moved the Supreme Court challenging Section 16 of The Chief Election Commissioner And Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions Of Service And Term Of Office) Act, 2023

articles.headline: Democrat from Kansas elected to US Senate for first time since 1932
articles.title: Democrat from Kansas elected to US Senate for first time since 1932
articles.description: A Democrat from Kansas has been elected to the US Senate for the first time in 94 years.

articles.headline: ‘We defeated Goliath’: Texas Democrat James Talarico wins Senate seat
articles.title: ‘We defeated Goliath’: Texas Democrat James Talarico wins Senate seat
articles.description: Democrat James Talarico wins the Texas Senate race in a historic midterm upset.

articles.headline: Trump-backed Vivek Ramaswamy loses Ohio gubernatorial race to Democrat Amy Acton
articles.title: Trump-backed Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy loses Ohio Governor’s race
articles.summary: Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy was defeated in Ohio by Democrat Amy Acton, who secured over 51% of the vote to become the state's first female governor. Ramaswamy, endorsed by President Donald Trump after previously advising him on government efficiency, pumped over $36 million of personal loans into the campaign. The 41-year-old businessman conceded the race on November 4, 2026, expressing support for the incoming administration.
articles.description: Vivek Ramaswamy lost to Amy Acton, who became the first woman to be elected Governor of the state

articles.headline: Darline Graham loses South Carolina Senate race to Democrat
articles.title: South Carolina elects Democratic senator for first time in almost three decades
articles.summary: Republican candidate Darline Graham lost her United States Senate race, handing Democrats their first victory in South Carolina in 28 years. Former paediatrician Annie Andrews won the contest during midterm elections. Graham had been appointed in July following the death of her brother, Senator Lindsey Graham, and faced scrutiny during her campaign after admitting she lacked familiarity with national security matters.
articles.description: Annie Andrews is projected to defeat Darline Graham, who was handpicked by President Trump to take her brother's seat after his death.

articles.headline: Democrat Abdul el-Sayed wins United States Senate seat in Michigan
articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed defeats Mike Rogers to win US Senate seat in Michigan
articles.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in the race for a United States Senate seat in Michigan, succeeding retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters. The 42-year-old former Wayne County health director campaigned on progressive policies including Medicare for All and curbing corporate influence. Although the victory maintains the current Senate balance, his populist platform drew significant national attention and campaign spending.
articles.description: The Democrat prevailed after a stream of Islamophobic rhetoric from top Republicans and a turbulent end to his campaign.

articles.headline: Spanish transport minister resigns following deadly train crash in Castilla-La Mancha
articles.title: Spanish transport minister resigns after train crash killed 69 people
articles.summary: Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente resigned and withdrew from the upcoming general election following a high-speed train collision in central Spain that killed 69 people. The crash occurred when a Renfe state-owned train struck a stationary private Iryo train after controllers authorized travel despite a signal failure. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced a 30-million-euro aid package to compensate victims and bereaved families.
articles.description: Oscar Puente says he could not 'continue in office' after two major train accidents in less than a year.

articles.headline: Florida Republicans fend off Democratic challenges and elect Byron Donalds governor
articles.title: Florida Republicans fend off Democrats as state elects first black governor
articles.summary: Republican candidate Byron Donalds was projected to win the Florida gubernatorial election on Tuesday, replacing term-limited Governor Ron DeSantis. Fellow Republican Ashley Moody also successfully defended her Senate seat against Democrat Angie Nixon. The victories occurred despite broader historic Democratic gains that secured full control of the United States Congress.
articles.description: Republican Byron Donalds, who was backed by President Donald Trump, will be the first black governor of Florida.

articles.headline: Democrat Troy Jackson secures Maine Senate seat after defeating Susan Collins.
articles.title: Democrat Troy Jackson wins Maine US Senate seat in blow to Republicans
articles.summary: Democratic candidate Troy Jackson defeated longtime Republican incumbent Susan Collins to capture a United States Senate seat in Maine, ending a nearly thirty-year tenure. The highly contested race attracted heavy spending from outside groups. Collins conceded on Wednesday, marking a significant political shift in the northeastern state as voters weighed economic pressures and national political alignments.
articles.description: Longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins had held the seat for three decades, but was swept away in the blue wave.

articles.headline: South Africans head to polls for local elections amid declining ANC support.
articles.title: South Africans vote in local elections seen as test for embattled ANC
articles.summary: South African voters cast ballots in crucial municipal elections on Wednesday to choose councils across eight metropolitan areas, forty-four districts, and two hundred five local regions. The vote serves as a major test for the governing African National Congress following losses in recent national contests. Turnout and security remain key focal points as the nation anticipates coalition outcomes and final results by Sunday.
articles.description: Municipal failures have contributed to declining public trust, President Cyril Ramaphosa has admitted.

articles.headline: Democrats win majorities in US House and Senate in midterms
articles.title: Anthony Zurcher: Democrats push deep into Trump heartland on historic night
articles.summary: In the midterm elections, the Democratic Party captured majorities in both the United States House of Representatives and the Senate by flipping multiple seats across states like Texas, Kansas, and Maine. President Donald Trump, whose second-term approval ratings dropped, faced substantial losses as voters rejected his administration's policies. Despite Republican defeats, conservatives maintained control in a few areas, while newly elected Democratic majorities prepared to counter presidential legislative agendas.
articles.description: Two Senate races that a year ago were thought to be battlegrounds turned out to be slam-dunks for the Democrats.

articles.headline: Democrat Amy Acton makes history in Ohio
articles.title: Democrat Amy Acton makes history in Ohio
articles.description: Democrat Amy Acton defeats Republican Vivek Ramaswamy to become the first ever woman to be elected as governor in Ohio.

articles.headline: Supreme Court questions relevance of two-child norm amid declining fertility
articles.title: Supreme Court judgment questions two-child norm with falling fertility rate
articles.summary: On November 4, 2026, a Supreme Court bench headed by Justice P.S. Narasimha ruled that laws penalising families with more than two children have lost relevance due to India's total fertility rate dropping to 1.9. The Court noted that such demographic shifts could lead to an aging population and referred the legal question regarding election eligibility criteria to a larger bench, highlighting concerns over reproductive autonomy and political representation.
articles.description: The Court noted that India’s total fertility rate has fallen from 3 to 1.9. A total rate of 2.1, known as the replacement rate, would allow one generation to completely replace itself

articles.headline: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries hails midterm victory
articles.title: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries hails midterm victory
articles.description: Top US Democratic politician Hakeem Jeffries has called the midterm results the start of a ‘great American comeback’.

articles.headline: India says structured mechanism remains in place ahead of Ganga Water Treaty expiry
articles.title: Weeks before expiry of Ganga Water Treaty, MEA says ‘structured mechanism’ remains in place for pact
articles.summary: Weeks before the bilateral agreement expires on December 12, 2026, the Ministry of External Affairs stated that the Joint Rivers Commission acts as the structured mechanism for cross-boundary water talks. During a briefing on November 3, 2026, spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal noted that India invited Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to New Delhi, though no renewal update exists. The pact was originally signed in 1996 by then Prime Ministers H.D. Deve Gowda and Sheikh Hasina.
articles.description: MEA official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterates that India has invited the Bangladesh Prime Minister to visit New Delhi but that there is neither any ‘update’ on the treaty’s renewal nor on the dates for the trip

articles.headline: Progressive candidates win New York congressional seats as Hochul is re-elected
articles.title: Democrats dominate NYC races, Hochul re-elected New York governor
articles.summary: Democratic candidates endorsed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani secured decisive victories in congressional races across New York on Tuesday. Governor Kathy Hochul also won re-election against Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman, forming the state's first all-woman executive ticket with Lieutenant Governor Adrienne Adams. The midterm outcomes reflect a growing progressive political shift within the region.
articles.description: Brad Lander, Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez sweep their congressional races in key Democratic districts.

articles.headline: North Korea fires multiple missiles following US allegations over crypto theft
articles.title: N Korea fires multiple missiles, denies US claims on Binance hack
articles.summary: North Korea launched several missiles toward the Sea of Japan on Wednesday, according to South Korea's military. The tests occurred shortly after Pyongyang dismissed an FBI announcement blaming North Korean hackers for a record six billion dollar cryptocurrency heist from Binance. Kim Yo Jong rejected future dialogue with Washington, citing ongoing hostile policies.
articles.description: Kim Yo Jong refuses dialogue with US after denying responsibility for theft of more than $6bn in crypto assets.

articles.headline: Democrat Josh Turek flips Iowa Senate seat by defeating Ashley Hinson
articles.title: Democrat Josh Turek flips Iowa Senate seat
articles.summary: Democrat Josh Turek won election to the United States Senate on Tuesday, defeating Republican Representative Ashley Hinson in Iowa. Turek's victory successfully flips a seat previously held by retiring Republican Senator Joni Ernst, boosting Democratic efforts to retake control of the Senate in a state that consistently favored Republicans.
articles.description: Turek beat Republican Ashley Hinson, a US House member.

articles.headline: Delhi records very poor air quality with severe pollution pockets
articles.title: Many parts of Delhi reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.summary: Delhi air quality remained in the very poor category on Wednesday morning, with several areas recording severe pollution levels according to Central Pollution Control Board data. The city registered a twenty-four-hour average Air Quality Index of 379 at nine in the morning, while neighboring northern cities also suffered from hazardous atmospheric conditions.
articles.description: The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 379 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on November 4, 2026, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data

articles.headline: IndiaAI Mission releases indigenous foundation models EKA-1 and Dhīr
articles.title: IndiaAI Mission releases indigenous foundation models EKA-1, Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B
articles.summary: The IndiaAI Mission released the EKA-1 model by Soket Labs Technology and Research alongside Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B by ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations on November 4, 2026. According to the government, the models enhance technological autonomy and enable offline-capable automation across various sectors. Built for Indian languages, banking, and cybersecurity, EKA-1 features 26.3 billion parameters, while ZenteiQ's open-source models support secure on-premise multilingual assistant deployments.
articles.description: These three indigenous models are a key milestone under the IndiaAI Mission, showcasing India's progress in creating homegrown AI technology

articles.headline: Keisha Lance Bottoms wins Georgia governor race to make history
articles.title: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms becomes first Black woman Governor in U.S.
articles.summary: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won the Georgia gubernatorial election on November 3, 2026, defeating Republican Rick Jackson and becoming the first Black woman elected governor in any US state. Media projections from CNN and NBC News confirmed the outcome, which returns the governor office to Democrats after two decades. President Donald Trump endorsed Jackson, while Barack Obama campaigned for Bottoms.
articles.description: Lance Bottoms defeated billionaire health care executive Rick Jackson, the Republican candidate. Outgoing Republican Governor Brian Kemp was term-limited and could not run again

articles.headline: Adam Hamilton becomes first Democratic senator in Kansas since 1932
articles.title: Kansas elects first Democratic senator in almost a century
articles.summary: Democrat Adam Hamilton defeated incumbent Republican Roger Marshall to win a US Senate seat in Kansas, according to Associated Press projections on November 3, 2026. The contest marked the first Democratic Senate win in the state since 1932. The Associated Press reported that the 110 million dollar race was the most expensive in state history, drawing involvement from Donald Trump.
articles.description: Adam Hamilton beat Republican Roger Marshall in a highly competitive race.

articles.headline: Amy Acton defeats Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio governor election
articles.title: Democrat Amy Acton beats Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio governor’s race
articles.summary: Democrat Amy Acton defeated Republican Vivek Ramaswamy to become the next governor of Ohio on November 3, 2026, marking the first time a woman was elected to the office and the first Democratic win since 2006. Acton, a physician and former state health official, faced a campaign featuring spending that topped 100 million dollars and a controversial television advertisement involving her estranged mother.
articles.description: Acton is the first Democrat to become governor of Ohio since 2006.

articles.headline: Sherrod Brown wins return to US Senate representing Ohio
articles.title: Sherrod Brown, an Ohio Democrat, wins return to US Senate
articles.summary: Democrat Sherrod Brown won a return to the US Senate on November 3, 2026, defeating incumbent Republican Jon Husted in a race projected by the Associated Press. Over 500 million dollars was spent on advertising in the contest, making it among the most expensive in US history. Brown focused on labor ties to regain the seat and will serve out the remainder of a term running until January 2029.
articles.description: More than $500m was spent on the contest, making it one of the most expensive Senate races in US history.

articles.headline: James Talarico wins Texas Senate race in historic Democratic victory
articles.title: Talarico wins Senate race, ending decades of Republican dominance in Texas
articles.summary: James Talarico secured a historic victory in the United States Senate race in Texas, marking the first time a Democrat won state office since 1994. The outcome followed heavy primary intervention by President Donald Trump and record-breaking spending. Meanwhile, Gina Hinojosa won the gubernatorial race to become the first Latino governor in state history, dealing a major blow to outgoing Governor Greg Abbott and his conservative policies.
articles.description: Democrats celebrate Talarico's and Hinojosa's victories, redefining Texas politics after decades of Republican reign.

articles.headline: Annie Andrews flips South Carolina Senate seat in major upset
articles.title: Democrat Annie Andrews flips South Carolina’s Senate seat
articles.summary: South Carolina elected a Democrat to the United States Senate for the first time since 1998, with Annie Andrews defeating Darline Graham in a Republican stronghold. Andrews raised more than $22m primarily through grassroots donations. Graham, appointed after her brother Senator Lindsey Graham died in July, struggled to unite conservatives despite receiving an endorsement from President Donald Trump during the campaign.
articles.description: Andrews beats Republican incumbent Darline Graham, sister of the late Senator Lindsey Graham, in a major upset.

articles.headline: Ossoff wins reelection in Georgia holding Senate seat for Democrats
articles.title: Ossoff wins reelection in Georgia holding Senate seat for Democrats
articles.description: Jon Ossoff has been reelected to the Senate in Georgia holding on to a key seat for the Democrats.

articles.headline: Democrat Roy Cooper celebrates flipping North Carolina Senate seat
articles.title: Democrat Roy Cooper celebrates flipping North Carolina Senate seat
articles.description: Former North Carolina Governor Roy Cooper celebrated his Senate victory in Raleigh

articles.headline: Hackers target supermarket refrigeration systems across European countries
articles.title: EU urges action as Germany, Romania and UK report supermarket cyberattacks
articles.summary: Cyberattacks raised refrigeration temperatures at supermarkets in Germany, Romania and the United Kingdom, bringing the total number of affected European countries to at least eleven. The European Union promised a collective response to the incidents, which spoiled food supplies. Cybersecurity officials noted that the attacks appeared semi-amateurish and stated there was no suspicion of involvement by a state actor.
articles.description: EU says supermarket hacks in at least 11 countries are 'not isolated', but a Romanian official suspects no state actor.

articles.headline: U.S. has no immediate plans to strike Iran, Trump says
articles.title: Trump says U.S. has no immediate plan to strike Iran: report
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated that his administration holds no immediate plans to strike Iran. Speaking to the Financial Times during a telephone interview on November 3, 2026, Mr. Trump expressed contentment regarding the current standoff. He remarked that the U.S. appears to be achieving all its objectives, signaling a stable diplomatic and military approach in the region.
articles.description: “We ‌seem to be getting everything we want,” ‌he told FT

articles.headline: Jon Ossoff wins re-election to US Senate in Georgia
articles.title: Democratic rising star Ossoff projected to hold Georgia seat
articles.summary: Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff defeated Republican challenger Mike Collins in Georgia during the midterm elections, securing a victory that reinforces Democratic presence in the swing state. Ossoff campaigned heavily on the rising cost of living and affordability concerns. The outcome contributes to the broader congressional battle shaping President Donald Trump's administration.
articles.description: Ossoff is seen as a potential leading contender for the Democratic nomination for president in 2028 if he throws his hat in the ring.

articles.headline: Keisha Lance Bottoms becomes Georgia's first Black woman governor
articles.title: Keisha Lance Bottoms makes history as first Black woman elected US governor
articles.summary: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms secured a historic victory by becoming the first Black woman elected governor in the United States, defeating billionaire Republican opponent Rick Jackson on November 3, 2026. Supported by a strong turnout from the state's Black voting bloc, the former Atlanta mayor and Joe Biden adviser succeeds outgoing Republican Governor Brian Kemp, who departs due to term limits.
articles.description: Bottoms, a former adviser to former President Joe Biden, beat Republican Rick Jackson to win the Georgia governor's race

articles.headline: Democrat Roy Cooper flips North Carolina Senate seat
articles.title: U.S. midterm elections: Democrat Roy Cooper flips Republican-held US Senate seat in North Carolina
articles.summary: Democrat Roy Cooper captured North Carolina’s United States Senate seat on November 3, 2026, defeating Trump-backed Republican Michael Whatley, according to media projections. Cooper, a former two-term governor, will succeed retiring Republican Senator Thom Tillis. The victory provides Democrats with a vital pickup in their ongoing battle against the Republican 53-47 Senate majority to gain control of the congressional chamber.
articles.description: Cooper, a well-known former two-term Governor, ‌defeated a hand-picked candidate of President Donald Trump after campaigning ‌on the high cost ‌of ⁠food and energy as ⁠Mr. Trump’s approval ratings fell

articles.headline: Democrat Roy Cooper wins North Carolina Senate race
articles.title: Democrat Roy Cooper flips North Carolina US Senate seat
articles.summary: Democrat Roy Cooper secured victory in North Carolina’s United States Senate race, delivering a major pickup for his party in the ongoing legislative battle. Cooper defeated former Republican National Committee chairman Michael Whatley. The former governor becomes the first Democrat elected to one of the state senate seats since 2008, succeeding outgoing Republican Senator Thom Tillis in office.
articles.description: Roy Cooper beat out Republican Michael Whatley.

articles.headline: Jon Ossoff wins re-election in Georgia Senate contest
articles.title: Jon Ossoff wins Georgia Senate race, defeating Republican Mike Collins
articles.summary: Democratic United States Senator Jon Ossoff won re-election in Georgia, defeating Republican Congressman Mike Collins in a marquee contest. Ossoff, who has served since 2021, campaigned on affordability, healthcare, and accountability. According to the Associated Press news agency, Ossoff held a substantial lead with 56 percent of votes counted, securing a critical victory for Democrats in the southern Republican stronghold.
articles.description: Ossoff is re-elected to a second term, winning a key seat for Democrats as the party tries to retake the Senate.

articles.headline: US Department of Justice expands Alaska Senate election probe
articles.title: US Department of Justice expands its probe into Alaska’s US Senate election
articles.summary: The United States Department of Justice intensified its investigation into an Alaska Senate race, issuing target letters to individuals including attorney Marc Elias. Officials allege Democrats fielded a sham candidate to confuse voters and defeat Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. Elias criticized the probe as politically motivated, while prosecutors have issued over one hundred subpoenas.
articles.description: The Trump administration is doubling down on allegations Democrats stood up a 'spoiler' candidate against Republicans.

articles.headline: Israel attorney general asks intelligence services for poll fraud proof
articles.title: Israel attorney general asks intel services to provide proof of poll fraud
articles.summary: Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara requested that the Shin Bet intelligence agency provide evidence regarding alleged electoral fraud by Arab Israeli parties. Baharav-Miara stated no proof had been submitted despite reports that Shin Bet head David Zini sought to question party leaders. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party accused the attorney general of obstructing the investigation.
articles.description: Head of Shin Bet, David Zini, a close associate of Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, had requested to question the leaders of the Arab parties as part of an investigation

articles.headline: President Zelenskyy says US elections will impact war in Ukraine
articles.title: President Zelenskyy says US elections will impact war in Ukraine
articles.description: Ukrainian President Volodmyr Zelenskyy has said that the US midterm elections will impact the ongoing war in his country

articles.headline: Texas voters cast ballots in record-breaking US Senate race
articles.title: Texans vote in most expensive Senate race in US history
articles.summary: Texas voters cast ballots in a consequential United States Senate race between Republican candidate Ken Paxton and Democratic candidate James Talarico on Tuesday, November 3. At least $573.2m was spent on the election, making it the most expensive in United States history, driven by outside donations including millions from billionaire Elon Musk.
articles.description: Pivotal Texas race for US Senate breaks spending records, with $573.2m poured into Paxton and Talarico campaigns.

articles.headline: NDA sweeps Urban Local Body elections in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: What NDA’s clean sweep in local body polls means for Andhra Pradesh politics
articles.summary: The National Democratic Alliance comprising the Telugu Desam Party, Jana Sena Party, and Bharatiya Janata Party has swept the Urban Local Body elections in Andhra Pradesh. The polls concluded following sporadic violence during nominations and voting. Minister Nara Lokesh noted that the outcome matched the landslide victory achieved by the alliance during the 2024 Andhra Pradesh Assembly polls.
articles.description: NDA’s thumping success in the local body elections is on the expected line, say political analysts, adding that though results show no hint of anti-incumbency, the alliance partners need to focus on ironing out the rifts

articles.headline: Survey reveals specific migration corridors from northeastern states to southern India
articles.title: Some northeast districts have their own migration corridors for jobs in southern India, reveals survey
articles.summary: A survey conducted by Seven Sisters Development Assistance across 14 administrative blocks in Assam, Meghalaya, and Tripura revealed distinct migration corridors for employment in southern India. Published on November 5, 2026, the study covered 693 households, noting that 88 percent of individuals migrated due to local job shortages. Karnataka emerged as the top destination, attracting 22.7 percent of the outflow. Researchers found that median monthly earnings stood at 15,000 rupees, with personal networks rather than formal institutions driving the relocations.
articles.description: The study by a Guwahati-based non-profit development organisation says 91% of the respondents across three States cited a “push” factor, such as shortage of land for farming or the need to repay loans, behind migration

articles.headline: Netanyahu’s eight-seat problem
articles.title: Netanyahu’s eight-seat problem
articles.description: Netanyahu’s Likud-led bloc won the most seats in the general election, but forming a government is another battle

articles.headline: Supreme Court reviews High Powered Enquiry Committee findings on police brutality
articles.title: ‘Very few complaints’ received so far on police brutality during July 20 protests, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court noted on November 5, 2026, that the High Powered Enquiry Committee received very few complaints regarding police brutality during the July 20 protests. The crackdown by Delhi Police on a Cockroach Janta Party demonstration caused numerous injuries, leading patients to seek treatment at Lady Hardinge Medical College and Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. The apex court permitted petitioners to submit additional video evidence directly to the inquiry panel.
articles.description: The Court allowed the petitioners the liberty to forward whatever material they have, including video clips, to the HPEC for its consideration

articles.headline: Ramayana film adaptation premieres worldwide with high production costs and mixed reviews
articles.title: India's costliest film retells a beloved Hindu epic - but divides critics
articles.summary: Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the high-budget film Ramayana: Rise of a Legend has opened globally following a massive 500 million dollar production. The movie features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram and Yash as Ravana, incorporating visual effects from DNEG and musical scores by AR Rahman and Hans Zimmer. Critics offered contrasting opinions, with NDTV rating it three out of five stars while The Guardian awarded four stars, praising its spectacular scale and ambitious narrative scope.
articles.description: Easily the most anticipated Bollywood film of the year, Ramayana: Rise of a Legend is the first of two parts.

articles.headline: Coal pile collapse kills three women and injures three in Jharkhand
articles.title: Three killed, 3 injured as coal pile collapses in Jharkhand’s Kathara colliery
articles.summary: Three women died and three others sustained injuries after a heap of coal collapsed at Central Coalfield Limited's Kathara colliery located in the Bokaro district of Jharkhand. According to Bokaro Deputy Commissioner Ajay Nath Jha, the tragic accident occurred around 5 a.m. when the victims were collecting coal from the site. A Central Coalfield Limited official stated that the incident involved coal theft.
articles.description: The Central Coalfield Limited official said it was a case of coal theft

articles.headline: Amit Shah criticizes Rahul Gandhi at Karnal rally over parliamentary disruptions
articles.title: Amit Shah at Karnal rally says Rahul Gandhi creating ‘ruckus’ culture in Parliament
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah accused Rahul Gandhi of fostering a culture of parliamentary disruption and boycotts within the Congress party during a rally in Karnal. Leading the Bharatiya Janata Party march, Mr. Shah also alleged that the opposition leader promotes anarchy and challenged him regarding his foreign visits. The campaign follows recent political tensions between the ruling party and the opposition INDIA bloc over electoral rolls.
articles.description: The Home Minister, who led the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' march in Karnal, accused the Congress leader of spreading anarchy in the country

articles.headline: Kerala High Court grants anticipatory bail to judge in car crash probe
articles.title: Cheranalloor crash: Kerala HC grants anticipatory bail to judge whose minor son allegedly drove luxury car
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court granted anticipatory bail to an Additional Judge whose minor son allegedly drove his luxury car into a scooter, causing the death of a 55-year-old man in Kochi on October 25. Justice Kauser Edappagath noted that the judicial officer fully cooperated with a six-hour police interrogation and home search. The judge's counsel stated that the boy took the vehicle without his father's knowledge.
articles.description: Justice Kauser Edappagath observes that the Additional Judge, who was interrogated by the police for six hours, has all along cooperated with the probe

articles.headline: Victor Wembanyama scores 52 points to lead Spurs past Mavericks
articles.title: Wembanyama pours in career-high 52 points as Spurs edge Mavericks 112-111
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama recorded a career-high 52 points, 24 rebounds, and eight blocked shots, securing the winning free throw with 24.2 seconds remaining to lift the San Antonio Spurs to a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday. Kyrie Irving missed a final shot for Dallas, which suffered its second consecutive defeat despite Irving leading his team with 29 points in the tightly contested matchup.
articles.description: Victor Wembanyama had 24 rebounds and 52 points as the San Antonio Spurs recorded their sixth straight win in the NBA.

articles.headline: Christian delegation meets RSS leader over mob attacks in West Bengal
articles.title: Christian representatives meet West Bengal RSS leader over mob attacks on congregations and churches
articles.summary: A delegation from the Bangiya Christiya Pariseba met with Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh leader Jishnu Saha to address recent mob violence against churches and pastors in West Bengal. While the forum reported 60 hate crimes since May, the RSS leader called for investigations into both the attacks and allegations of forced religious conversions by Christian groups.
articles.description: Senior RSS functionary from West Bengal Jishnu Basu, the Saha Khetra Prachar Pramukh of South Bengal, said that dialogue will continue with the representatives of Christian organisations but there are genuine concerns about forced conversion

articles.headline: Jaishankar urges Commonwealth members to de-risk and diversify supply chains
articles.title: Jaishankar urges Commonwealth partners to 'de-risk and diversify'
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar attended the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in St. John's on November 3, 2026. Speaking at a business leaders meeting, he emphasized enhancing local distribution, connectivity corridors, and digital public infrastructure to drive growth. He also met with United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to discuss economic partnerships and trade agreements.
articles.description: S. Jaishankar said Commonwealth partners need to make more efforts to enhance local distribution, adding that more connectivity corridors are good for business

articles.headline: Amish Shah wins Arizona congressional race to become sixth Indian-American representative
articles.title: Amish Shah claims victory in Arizona, sixth Indian-American in U.S. House
articles.summary: Democratic physician Amish Shah won the election on November 4, 2026, for the United States House of Representatives in Arizona's First Congressional District. Defeating Republican Jay Feely with 52.49 percent of the vote, Dr. Shah made history as the first Indian-American to represent Arizona in Congress while successfully flipping a previously Republican-held seat.
articles.description: Amish Shah made history as he became the first Indian-American to represent Arizona in Congress. By defeating Feely, Mr. Shah flipped a Republican-held seat

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs Azam Khan to seek relief from Allahabad High Court
articles.title: Supreme Court asks Allahabad HC to give Azam Khan priority hearing
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India advised senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan to approach the Allahabad High Court regarding his recent arrest by the Directorate of Enforcement. The apex court requested a priority hearing on November 16. Khan, who faces numerous criminal cases, alleges political motivation behind his ongoing legal challenges in Uttar Pradesh.
articles.description: The Supreme Court has asked the High Court to hear the case on November 16; Azam Khan alleges “series of politically motivated cases”

articles.headline: Rajeev Chandrasekhar tells Rahul Gandhi to go to Bangladesh over alleged anarchy
articles.title: Keralam BJP chief Rajeev Chandrasekhar tells Rahul Gandhi to ‘go to Bangladesh’, accuses him of ‘creating anarchy’
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party Keralam president Rajeev Chandrasekhar told Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on November 5, 2026, to relocate to Bangladesh and accused him of attempting to create anarchy in India. Chandrasekhar asserted that Indian democracy is protected by citizens and alleged that Gandhi is trying to divert public attention amid protests over voter roll revisions and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
articles.description: In a Facebook post, Rajeev Chandrasekhar says Rahul Gandhi ‘can take along Jamaat-e-Islami, which supports him, and pursue politics there’

articles.headline: Michigan voters face crucial choice as Trump’s grip on Congress is tested
articles.title: Michigan voters face crucial choice as Trump’s grip on Congress is tested
articles.description: Michigan’s closely contested Senate race and voter concerns over the economy are putting Trump’s control of Washington.

articles.headline: International Court of Justice schedules Rohingya genocide ruling for November
articles.title: Top UN court to rule November 19 on Rohingya genocide case
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice will announce its decision on November nineteen regarding whether Myanmar's military crackdown on the Rohingya Muslim minority constitutes genocide. The case, brought by Gambia in twenty-twenty under the United Nations Genocide Convention, addresses severe violence that forced hundreds of thousands to flee to Bangladesh. Myanmar has consistently denied the allegations, maintaining its actions targeted armed insurgents.
articles.description: Judges at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) have for seven years been weighing accusations by The Gambia that Myanmar’s brutal repression of the Rohingya breached the 1948 UN Genocide Convention

articles.headline: South Korea to expand naval anti-piracy operations near Hormuz Strait
articles.title: South Korea plans to expand anti-piracy operations closer to Hormuz Strait
articles.summary: South Korea plans to extend its Cheonghae naval unit's operational area toward the Strait of Hormuz to protect economic interests. The Ministry of National Defense stated the mission remains noncombat and independent of allied forces. Opposition lawmakers expressed concerns that the expansion could draw the nation into the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran.
articles.description: Seoul proposes extending its Cheonghae unit’s patrols to waters near Oman’s Duqm amid US pressure over Iran war.

articles.headline: Delhi Police registers FIR over child abuse material on Meta platforms
articles.title: Delhi Police registers FIR over alleged circulation of child sexual abuse material on Meta platforms
articles.summary: The Delhi Police Special Cell registered an FIR on October 8 regarding the circulation of suspected child sexual abuse material on Facebook and Instagram. Officials are investigating approximately 10 flagged links under the Information Technology Act. The probe follows a complaint regarding the availability of such content on platforms operated by Meta India.
articles.description: Approximately 10 links were flagged in a complaint alleging the circulation of such material, following which the police initiated an investigation to verify the allegations, says an official

articles.headline: Germany’s Merz expects Trump to keep ignoring Congress
articles.title: Germany’s Merz expects Trump to keep ignoring Congress
articles.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz expects US President Donald Trump to keep bypassing Congress despite midterm losses.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate attaches assets linked to Reliance Anil Ambani Group
articles.title: ED action in Reliance Anil Ambani Group cases | Explained
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate has cumulatively seized or attached assets worth approximately 23,100 crore rupees in cases involving the Reliance Anil Ambani Group. On November 3, the agency attached an additional 510.17 crore rupees in assets related to alleged bank fraud cases involving Reliance Communications, Reliance Home Finance, and Reliance Commercial Finance under anti-money laundering laws.
articles.description: On November 3, the ED said it had attached assets worth ₹510.17 crore linked to the group in connection with alleged bank fraud cases against Reliance Communications Limited, Reliance Home Finance Limited and Reliance Commercial Finance Limited

articles.headline: Fenerbahce defeats Liverpool as Como records historic Champions League victory
articles.title: Champions League: Liverpool suffer 3-2 loss at Fenerbahce, Como thump Lens
articles.summary: Fenerbahce secured a 3-2 victory over Liverpool in the Champions League following Vedat Muriqi’s late winner. Meanwhile, Italian club Como achieved a historic 9-1 win against Lens, matching the competition's record for the largest victory margin. Elsewhere, Real Madrid defeated AEK Athens 3-2, while Manchester City and Arsenal also secured wins in their respective matches.
articles.description: Como equal Champions League record with stunning 9-1 win at Lens as Haaland rescues Manchester City at Leipzig.

articles.headline: Severe weather disrupts election day across several US states
articles.title: Severe weather disrupts election day across several US states
articles.description: Flash floods, torrential rain and tornadoes have disrupted midterm election day in several US states.

articles.headline: United States ends security assistance accord with Israel
articles.title: Trump says U.S. cutting $3.8 billion annual security assistance to Israel
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced on Tuesday the termination of a ten-year security assistance agreement that provided Israel with three point eight billion dollars annually. Trump stated that Israel no longer requires the financial support, adding that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu agreed with the decision. The move drew criticism from Israeli opposition politician Gadi Eisenkot over the handling of strategic relations.
articles.description: Donald Trump said Israel was “fine” with him ending the assistance, which began in 2019 and was signed under his predecessor, Barack Obama, three years earlier

articles.headline: Yemeni government accuses Iranian and Lebanese operatives of aiding Houthi forces
articles.title: Yemen gov’t accuses IRGC, Hezbollah of sending 21 experts to back Houthis
articles.summary: Yemen's internationally recognised government stated on Tuesday that fourteen members of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and seven members of Lebanon's Hezbollah have deployed to assist Houthi military operations. Interior Minister Major-General Ibrahim Haidan said these experts are directing planning across five provinces. Haidan urged the international community to designate the Houthis as terrorists and enforce United Nations arms embargoes.
articles.description: Yemeni interior minister says foreign involvement expanded beyond arms and training to directing military operations.

articles.headline: Cyclone Murasu brings heavy overnight rainfall to Telangana districts
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu impact on Telangana | Extremely heavy rains lash Bhadradri on November 4
articles.summary: Mandal areas in Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts recorded extremely heavy rainfall between 204 mm and 235 mm overnight due to cyclone Murasu, according to a report issued on November 4, 2026, by the Telangana Development Planning Society. The India Meteorological Department placed Bhadradri Kothagudem under an orange alert for heavy rain, while continuing showers caused accumulation reaching 88 mm in local mandals.

articles.headline: New Zealand general election shows parties neck and neck in polls
articles.title: New Zealand braces for knife-edge election: What you need to know
articles.summary: New Zealand is preparing for a general election on November 7, 2026, with polls showing Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National Party and the opposition Labour Party in a tight race. Operating under a mixed-member proportional system, neither major party is projected to win an outright majority, meaning smaller parties will likely determine the formation of the next coalition government.
articles.description: Smaller parties hold the key, with major contenders expected to fall short of the majority needed to govern alone.

articles.headline: OpenAI announces ChatGPT search volume reaches twenty percent of Google
articles.title: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
articles.summary: During a press event on Monday, OpenAI consumer product lead Adam Fry announced that search query volume through ChatGPT has reached twenty percent of Google. Fry stated that the company defines searches as queries resulting in web traffic, noting that ads have not negatively impacted product usage ahead of a potential initial public offering next year.
articles.description: In many circles, "Ask Chat" has replaced "Google it," and that's reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google. Adam Fry, OpenAI's consumer product lead for ChatGPT, made the announcement at a press event on Monday. He said […]

articles.headline: Indian-American candidates secure victories during United States midterm elections
articles.title: US midterm election results 2026: Key Indian-origin winners
articles.summary: Several Indian-origin candidates secured congressional victories as Democrats made gains in the United States midterm elections on November 4, 2026. Suhas Subramanyam won in Virginia and Pia Dandiya won in Florida for the House of Representatives, whereas Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy lost the Ohio gubernatorial race to Democrat Amy Acton.
articles.description: Indian-Americans Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives, while Vivek ‌Ramaswamy‌ was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor

articles.headline: Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian says return to war benefits no one
articles.title: Iran president says return to war benefits 'no one', after reported U.S. strikes
articles.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated on Tuesday that returning to conflict would benefit no one, following reported United States strikes on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari reported that indirect negotiations are ongoing, as Iranian officials indicated readiness to reopen the strategic waterway under specific conditions.
articles.description: It came as U.S. voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that threaten President Donald Trump's grip on power

articles.headline: Death toll rises to thirty one following Russian strike in Ukraine
articles.title: Death toll hits 31 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with dozens still missing
articles.summary: The death toll from a Russian attack on a humanitarian aid site in Komyshuvakha rose to thirty one on Tuesday, with more than forty five people missing. Regional military administration acting head Mykhailo Semikin reported that rescue teams continue searching the site, while President Volodymyr Zelenskyy noted that Russia launched hundreds of attack drones and missiles across nine regions.
articles.description: Teams of rescuers and volunteers continued to search the cratered blast site of a destroyed aid facility and shelter in Komyushuvakha

articles.headline: Jailed Indian scholar Sharjeel Imam triggers debate over minority representation and democracy
articles.title: Has India’s democracy failed its Muslims? Jailed scholar triggers debate
articles.summary: Sharjeel Imam, a 38-year-old Indian scholar imprisoned since January 2020, has sparked a national debate regarding the political representation of Muslims in India. In an interview from New Delhi prison with The Quint on September 29, Imam criticized the constitution and secular framework, drawing mixed reactions from legal scholars and academics regarding minority rights and systemic democracy.
articles.description: Sharjeel Imam questioned foundational ideas of India's nationalism in interview with The Quint, inspiring heated debate.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu approaches Supreme Court over unpaid Cauvery river water releases
articles.title: Tamil Nadu seeks urgent oral mentioning in Supreme Court over Cauvery water issue
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government made an urgent oral mentioning before the Supreme Court of India on November 5, 2026, accusing Karnataka of withholding Cauvery river water since October 23. Counsel B. Karunakaran told a Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant that four lakh hectares of crops are at risk because Karnataka failed to release 3,000 cusecs daily as ordered.
articles.description: The court agreed to list the plea early

articles.headline: Israeli opposition criticises Benjamin Netanyahu after Democrats win US Congress
articles.title: Israel’s opposition slams ‘toxic Netanyahu’ after Democrats win US Congress
articles.summary: Israeli opposition politicians criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday following Democratic majorities in the United States Congress. Yair Lapid and other leaders argued that Netanyahu has eroded bipartisan support and endangered security. Meanwhile, opposition figures pledged to restore relations with Washington, as Netanyahu did not immediately respond to the criticism regarding his governance and foreign policy stance.
articles.description: Netanyahu's rivals say US midterm results show Israel 'cannot afford' to have the prime minister remain in office.

articles.headline: AERB chairperson assures safety standards amid private nuclear sector entry
articles.title: Private sector participation in nuclear energy: No compromise on safety aspects, says AERB Chairperson
articles.summary: Atomic Energy Regulatory Board Chairperson A.K. Balasubrahmanian stated on November 5, 2026, that safety standards will not be compromised as private players enter India's nuclear energy sector. Speaking at a symposium organised by the Atomic Energy Retirees' Association, he explained that the sector is opening up to meet national power requirements while the board maintains strict regulatory enforcement.
articles.description: The AERB chairperson’s remarks gain significance in the context of SHANTI Act and the Union government’s policy decision to welcome private players

articles.headline: Google disables Search in schools that reject artificial intelligence features
articles.title: Google is entirely disabling Search in schools that don’t want AI
articles.summary: Alphabet subsidiary Google announced that access to Google Search and artificial intelligence tools like Gemini will be turned off in K-12 student accounts unless administrators explicitly enable them. According to Chris Phillips, Google education vice president, search and artificial intelligence are deeply integrated. The change follows scrutiny from lawmakers regarding artificial intelligence in schools and precedes a United States pilot of a guided learning feature.
articles.description: Google is completely turning off Search in schools that reject its AI features, the company told The New York Times. The decision was also shared in a broader education-related update from Google on Tuesday, saying that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search "will be entirely off" for K-12 student accounts […]

articles.headline: BAMUL increases prices of ghee, butter and paneer in Karnataka
articles.title: After milk and curd, prices of ghee, butter and paneer too up in Karnataka
articles.summary: Following previous hikes on milk and curd by the Karnataka Milk Federation, the Bangalore Urban, Rural & Ramanagara District Co-Operative Milk Producers Societies Union Limited raised prices for ghee, butter, and paneer across the state on November 4, 2026. Industry representatives warned that the adjustments create an additional financial strain for the local hospitality sector.
articles.description: The revised prices, released on November 4, will come into effect across the State on November 5

articles.headline: Russian strikes on Ukrainian aid center and hospital kill thirty eight
articles.title: Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital
articles.summary: Recent Russian attacks across Ukraine, including a glide bomb strike on an aid distribution center in Komyshuvakha and a hit on a Dnipro hospice, have killed at least thirty eight civilians over twenty four hours. Regional head Mykhailo Semikin noted the severe scale of the tragedy, while Ukrainian water supplier Kyivvodokanal reported total water supply cuts in Kyiv due to damaged energy infrastructure.
articles.description: At least 38 people are killed in 24 hours and Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky warns dozens more could be trapped under rubble.

articles.headline: Palghar villagers and opposition leaders continue fierce resistance against Vadhavan port project
articles.title: Vadhavan port project faces continued resistance from Palghar villagers
articles.summary: Villagers, farmers, and fishing communities gathered near Dahanu on Friday to protest the Vadhavan port project, backed by opposition politicians from parties like Congress and Shiv Sena. Protesters warned that the ₹76,220 crore initiative by the Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority and Maharashtra Maritime Board will destroy marine life, displace Adivasi lands, and threaten traditional livelihoods.
articles.description: Opposition parties have joined villagers in Palghar who say the ₹76,220-crore Vadhavan port will take their sea, their farms and their futures

articles.headline: Cyclone Murasu batters Andhra Pradesh, leaving two dead and extensive damage
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu batters A.P.; two dead, 52,459 hectares of crops damaged
articles.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu struck south coastal Andhra Pradesh, resulting in two fatalities after buildings collapsed in Bapatla district. Prakhar Jain of the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority stated that over 12,000 people sought shelter in rehabilitation facilities. The India Meteorological Department reported maximum sustained winds of 110 to 120 kilometers per hour during landfall near Ongole, causing widespread crop destruction and transport disruptions.
articles.description: Cyclone brings heavy rain to Prakasam and Palnadu districts; wind speed during landfall was 110-120 kmph, says IMD; 12,230 people are in rehabilitation centres in Guntur, Bapatla, and Palnadu districts; preliminary reports estimate losses of ₹344 crore

articles.headline: Israeli political deadlock persists as parliamentary majority remains elusive for blocs
articles.title: Israel political deadlock leaves Netanyahu’s future hanging in the balance
articles.summary: Israel faces political uncertainty as election certification approaches with neither major political bloc securing a parliamentary majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured 53 seats, while opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot obtained 48 seats. Opposition figures plan to form a national emergency government, though potential alliances with Arab-led lists or ultra-Orthodox factions remain uncertain ahead of the November 10 swearing-in ceremony.
articles.description: With neither bloc near a majority, Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties hold the key to Israel’s next government..

articles.headline: Volodymyr Zelenskyy hopes upcoming Abu Dhabi talks will lead to trilateral meeting
articles.title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy hopes Abu Dhabi talks will open path to Putin meeting
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed optimism that upcoming United States-mediated discussions in Abu Dhabi will pave the way for a trilateral meeting involving Russian President Vladimir Putin. Speaking in Berlin alongside German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Zelenskyy highlighted the diplomatic efforts scheduled for November 10 and 11. Meanwhile, European officials are holding separate talks in Brussels regarding post-war security architecture and ongoing financial support for Ukraine.
articles.description: Ukrainian president meets German chancellor in Berlin, who says Russia is yet to engage seriously in peace efforts.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate searches Aryan Hometec locations over alleged fraud
articles.title: Bengaluru cops can’t find builder accused of cheating, but ED does; raids three locations linked to Aryan Hometec in ₹90-crore fraud case
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate conducted raids at three locations linked to Aryan Hometec Private Limited, its directors Bharath Reddy, and Rashmi Bharath Reddy. Investigators seized records regarding an alleged ninety-crore rupee fraud and money laundering case. The agency accused the developers of cheating landowner B.G. Anjinappa, failing to deliver apartments, and diverting funds collected from homebuyers to family entities.
articles.description: The money laundering investigation was initiated based on multiple FIRs registered by the police following complaints from a landowner, homebuyers and financial institutions

articles.headline: Brazilian airport torn apart by violent storm
articles.title: Brazilian airport torn apart by violent storm
articles.description: Dramatic footage captured the moment a powerful tornado struck Chapecó Airport in Santa Catarina, Brazil

articles.headline: World record 53 red cards shown in Brazil football match
articles.title: World record 53 red cards shown in Brazil football match
articles.description: Referees have red-carded 53 players and staff after a massive brawl in an under-20s football match in Brazil.

articles.headline: Syrian security forces foil alleged Hezbollah plot targeting Homs oil refinery
articles.title: Syria says it foiled Hezbollah plot to target Homs oil refinery
articles.summary: Syrian security forces arrested members of a cell linked to Lebanon’s Hezbollah group for planning an attack on the Homs refinery. Hezbollah denied involvement, stating it maintains no presence in Syria. Separately, Syrian authorities announced arrests of suspected ISIL members in Deir Az Zor following recent infrastructure attacks across the country, according to state media reports.
articles.description: Hezbollah denies the Syrian accusations, reiterating that it does not have any presence on Syrian territory.

articles.headline: US midterm campaign spending reaches record twelve billion dollars amid cost concerns
articles.title: How US midterms have cost a record $12bn as cost of living soars
articles.summary: Candidates and outside political groups have spent nearly twelve billion dollars on the United States midterm elections, according to OpenSecrets. Critics argue that unregulated super PAC funding gives wealthy donors excessive influence during an election cycle dominated by affordability issues. Meanwhile, the lobbying group American Israel Public Affairs Committee has faced scrutiny for channeling millions through shell political action committees.
articles.description: Candidates, donors and super PACs are spending more than ever on political campaigns.

articles.headline: AERB chairperson promises no safety compromises in private nuclear sector
articles.title: Private sector participation in nuclear energy: No compromise on safety aspects, says AERB Chairperson
articles.summary: Atomic Energy Regulatory Board Chairperson A.K. Balasubrahmanian addressed concerns regarding private sector entry into India's nuclear energy sector. Speaking at a symposium organised by the Atomic Energy Retirees’ Association, he assured that safety and regulatory standards will not be diluted while providing an enabling environment for private players to meet the rising power demands of the country.
articles.description: The AERB chairperson’s remarks gain significance in the context of SHANTI Act and the Union government’s policy decision to welcome private players

articles.headline: Mississippi and Alaska Senate races remain uncalled following midterms
articles.title: What’s delaying the US Senate election results in Mississippi and Alaska?
articles.summary: The United States midterm elections concluded with Democrats securing congressional control, but Senate races in Mississippi and Alaska remain undecided as ballots are processed. Mississippi features a razor-thin margin between candidates Cindy Hyde-Smith and Scott Colom, while Alaska utilizes a ranked-choice voting system and faces legal disputes. State officials expect certified results to be finalised by mid-November.
articles.description: Ranked-choice voting may decide Alaska's Senate outcome, while Mississippi's race hangs on a knife's edge.

articles.headline: Tata Motors completes acquisition of Iveco Group in multibillion-euro deal
articles.title: Tata-Iveco €3.8-bn deal turns global ambition into reality; eyes cross-market expansion
articles.summary: Tata Motors completed its €3.8-billion acquisition of Iveco Group NV, creating a combined commercial vehicle enterprise with presence in over 130 countries. Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran announced that the merged entity will pursue cross-market expansion, introducing Iveco products in India and Tata vehicles in international markets supported by 27 manufacturing facilities.
articles.description: The road ahead is to move forward with a shared ambition of Tata Motors and Iveco Group NV to create a stronger, more innovative and more resilient commercial mobility enterprise

articles.headline: Israeli opposition leaders back Gadi Eisenkot to replace Benjamin Netanyahu
articles.title: Israel’s opposition leaders back Eisenkot to oust Netanyahu
articles.summary: Five opposition party leaders agreed to support former military chief Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister during a meeting in Herzliya. The bloc aims to rapidly replace Benjamin Netanyahu’s government before President Isaac Herzog begins coalition consultations. However, the opposition remains divided regarding potential alliances with Arab-led parties, whose combined nineteen seats could prove decisive in the one hundred twenty seat Knesset.
articles.description: Opposition promises to form a government quickly but remains split over whether to ally with Arab-led parties.

articles.headline: Delhi booth-level officers instructed to seek additional citizenship proof
articles.title: Delhi SIR: Aadhaar alone not enough, BLOs asked to seek ‘citizenship proof’ from voters
articles.summary: Booth-level officers across constituencies in the national capital are facing renewed scrutiny during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls. Officials reported being directed to collect further documents from electors who previously submitted only Aadhaar cards to establish citizenship, despite more than 94% of flagged cases having been marked for final rolls by the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer.
articles.description: Regarding those electors flagged for ‘no mapping’ notices, several BLOs claim that Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) were directing them to revisit voters and seek additional documents to establish that they were not ‘Bangladeshi’ or ‘Rohingya’

articles.headline: Black Sea commercial shipping targeted as Russia and Ukraine escalate attacks
articles.title: Global food security is under threat
articles.summary: Escalating drone strikes by Russia and Ukraine on commercial vessels and port infrastructure in the Black Sea and Danube region have severely disrupted global grain exports and threatened food security. The attacks have knocked out significant export capacities for both nations, driving up international wheat futures and raising diplomatic tensions with NATO member states over maritime security.
